Moreover, assume that there is a surjective qcqs map X → Y from a locally spatial diamond X. Then Y is locally spatial. (The existence of such a surjective qcqs map from a locally spatial diamond is automatic if Y is quasicompact.)
items.note: Not named in any node statement; it is the fibrewise criterion used in Propositions 13.4(v) and 13.12, which nodes DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/relative-representability and DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/reduction-to-spatial-and-hausdorff-cohomology state; covered by D5 description: 'Construct representability in diamonds and in locally spatial diamonds, including the different pro-étale and v-locality assumptions in §13 … The source index assigns §13 here'. Proof uses Proposition 12.3. See source issue (U/V swapped in the proof).

items.name: Proposition 13.6: fibre criterion for separated quasi-pro-étale maps (Fargues)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of v-stacks. Then f is quasi-pro-étale if and only if it is representable in locally spatial diamonds and for all complete algebraically closed (nonarchimedean) fields C with a map Spa(C, O_C) → Y, the pullback Y′ ×_Y Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C, O_C) is pro-étale.
items.note: D5 description: 'Prove the fibre criterion for separated quasi-pro-étale morphisms'. Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/relative-representability cites 'Proposition 13.6 with proof'. Proof uses Proposition 13.4(iv), 11.24, Lemma 7.19 and Proposition 11.30.

items.name: Definition 13.7: Berkovich space |X|_B of an affinoid perfectoid space
items.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space, and fix a topologically nilpotent unit ϖ ∈ R. The Berkovich space |X|_B is the space of all multiplicative bounded nonarchimedean seminorms |·| : R → ℝ_{≥0} with |ϖ| = 1/2, equipped with the weakest topology making the functions f ↦ |f| continuous for all f ∈ R.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/berkovich-quotient states it. Nearest library layer: mathlib:MulRingSeminorm and mathlib:IsNonarchimedean give the seminorm notion, but no Berkovich spectrum of a perfectoid Tate ring.

items.name: Remark 13.8 and following: comparison maps |X|_B ⇄ |X|
items.statement: |X|_B is canonically independent of the choice of ϖ. There is a natural map |X|_B → |X| (a multiplicative bounded nonarchimedean seminorm is in particular a valuation), and a map |X| → |X|_B: for x ∈ X with Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺), K(x) carries a nonarchimedean norm unique up to scaling, normalised by |ϖ| = 1/2, and R → K(x) → ℝ_{≥0} is a point of |X|_B. The composite |X|_B → |X| → |X|_B is the identity. (The map |X|_B → |X| is not continuous.)
items.locator: Remark 13.8 and the paragraph after it, p. 79, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/berkovich-quotient ('the map |X|_B -> |X| is a section but is not continuous'). Independence of ϖ is deduced from Proposition 13.9.

items.name: Proposition 13.9: |X|_B is the maximal Hausdorff quotient of |X|
items.statement: Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space. The topological space |X|_B is compact Hausdorff, and the map |X| → |X|_B is a continuous map identifying |X|_B as the maximal Hausdorff quotient of |X|.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/berkovich-quotient. Nearest library layer: mathlib:T2Quotient (the largest Hausdorff quotient, with universal property T2Quotient.lift); the identification with |X|_B is not in the library. Quotient-map step uses Lemma 2.6.

items.name: Proposition 13.10: the functor Y ↦ |Y|_B on small v-sheaves
items.statement: There is a unique colimit-preserving functor Y ↦ |Y|_B from small v-sheaves to topological spaces extending X ↦ |X|_B on affinoid perfectoid spaces. It comes with natural transformations |Y|_B → |Y| → |Y|_B whose composite is the identity, and the map |Y| → |Y|_B is continuous and a quotient map. (Explicitly, |Y|_B is the subset of |Y| of points representable by maps Spa(K, O_K) → Y, with the quotient topology from |X|_B for any surjection X → Y from a disjoint union of affinoid perfectoid spaces.)
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/berkovich-quotient.

items.name: Proposition 13.11: |Y|_B for qcqs Y is compact Hausdorff and the maximal Hausdorff quotient
items.statement: Let Y be a qcqs (small) v-sheaf. Then |Y|_B is a compact Hausdorff space, and it is the maximal Hausdorff quotient of |Y|.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/berkovich-quotient ('for Y qcqs, |Y|_B is compact Hausdorff and is the maximal Hausdorff quotient of |Y|'). Proof first for spatial diamonds Y = X/R with X, R affinoid perfectoid, then for Y = X/R with X, R spatial.

items.name: Proposition 13.12: Y → |Y|_B is representable in locally spatial diamonds
items.statement: Let Y be a quasicompact separated diamond. Then the map Y → |Y|_B (to the v-sheaf of the compact Hausdorff space |Y|_B) is representable in locally spatial diamonds.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/reduction-to-spatial-and-hausdorff-cohomology. Proof: profinite cover S → |Y|_B, Proposition 13.4(iv), Lemma 13.5, reduction to |Y|_B a point, then Y is spatial via Spa(C, C⁺)/G (Lemma 10.13, Propositions 11.24, 11.20, 12.15, and forward reference Proposition 18.7).

items.name: Proposition 13.13: cohomology of |Y|_B is computed on |Y|
items.statement: Let Y be a quasicompact separated diamond, and consider the map f : |Y| → |Y|_B. Then pullback f^* induces a fully faithful functor D⁺(|Y|_B, ℤ) → D⁺(|Y|, ℤ). In particular, for any abelian sheaf F on |Y|_B, one has Hⁱ(|Y|_B, F) ≅ Hⁱ(|Y|, f^*F).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/reduction-to-spatial-and-hausdorff-cohomology; D5 description: '§13 … including its ordinary sheaf-cohomology assertion 13.13, proved using D0'. Proof: stalks of Rf_*f^*F are RΓ(f⁻¹(y), F_y) and f⁻¹(y) is the closure of a rank-one point, a spectral space with a unique generic point ([Sta, Tag 02UW]).

items.name: Definition 14.1(i): the étale site Y_ét of a locally spatial diamond
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack on Perf which is a locally spatial diamond. The étale site Y_ét is the site whose objects are (locally separated) étale maps Y′ → Y, with coverings given by families of jointly surjective maps, where surjectivity refers to surjectivity as v-stacks on Perf.
items.note: C0: 'Construct the étale site of a locally spatial diamond … (14.1). Use the stated locally separated convention.' DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Definition 14.1(ii): the quasi-pro-étale site Y_qproét of a diamond
items.statement: Let Y be a diamond. The quasi-pro-étale site Y_qproét is the site whose objects are (locally separated) quasi-pro-étale maps Y′ → Y, with coverings given by families of jointly surjective maps (as v-stacks on Perf). There are cutoff variants Y_qproét,κ, and one always restricts to small sheaves.
items.locator: Definition 14.1(ii) and following paragraph, pp. 81–82, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: C0 (14.1). DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Definition 14.1(iii): the v-site Y_v of a small v-stack
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack on Perf. The v-site Y_v is the site whose objects are all maps Y′ → Y from small v-sheaves Y′, with coverings given by families of jointly surjective maps (as v-stacks on Perf; for perfectoid X and {X_i → X} this means a v-cover). There are cutoff variants Y_v,κ, and one always restricts to small sheaves.
items.locator: Definition 14.1(iii) and following paragraph, pp. 81–82, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: C0 (14.1). DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. The ordinary v-site of Perf is DiamondsAndVStacks:D2.

items.name: Proposition 14.2: the three topoi are algebraic; qc/qs objects
items.statement: The categories of (small) sheaves on Y_ét, resp. Y_qproét, resp. Y_v, for Y a locally spatial diamond, resp. a diamond, resp. a small v-stack, are algebraic (topoi). If Y is 0-truncated (i.e. a small v-sheaf), then an object is quasicompact, resp. quasiseparated, if and only if it is quasicompact, resp. quasiseparated, as a small v-stack on Perf.
items.note: Proof 'left to the reader' in the source. C0: 'Prove algebraicity/coherence in the appropriate size setting'. Algebraic/coherent topos interfaces: DiamondsAndVStacks:D0. DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Proposition 14.3: Y_ét has enough points (geometric points Spa(C, C⁺))
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond. Then the étale site Y_ét has enough points. More precisely, for any y ∈ |Y|, choose a quasi-pro-étale map y : Spa(C(y), C(y)⁺) → Y where C(y) is algebraically closed and C(y)⁺ ⊂ C(y) is an open and bounded valuation subring, such that y maps the closed point to y. Then F ↦ F_y = colim_{y→U∈Y_ét} F(U) defines a point of the topos Y_ét^∼, and a section s ∈ F(Y) of a sheaf F on Y_ét is zero if and only if s_y = 0 for all y ∈ |Y|.
items.note: C0: 'enough geometric points'. DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Target interface in Mathlib: mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point and mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.HasEnoughPoints. The analogous statement for analytic adic spaces is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points (not the diamond statement).

items.name: Morphisms of sites λ_Y : Y_v → Y_qproét and ν_Y : Y_qproét → Y_ét
items.statement: If Y is a diamond there is a morphism of sites λ_Y : Y_v → Y_qproét, and if Y is a locally spatial diamond a morphism of sites ν_Y : Y_qproét → Y_ét; the underlying functors go the other way (an étale map is quasi-pro-étale; a quasi-pro-étale map has source a small v-sheaf). They commute with all finite limits, hence define morphisms of topoi, with pullbacks ν_Y^* : Y_ét^∼ → Y_qproét^∼ and λ_Y^* : Y_qproét^∼ → Y_v^∼ on categories of small sheaves (the latter two categories being the large filtered colimits over κ of Y_qproét,κ^∼, resp. Y_v,κ^∼).
items.note: C0: 'Construct the morphisms of topoi, their pullbacks and units/counits.' DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Lemma 14.4: λ_Y^* (and f^* on quasi-pro-étale topoi) commutes with all small limits
items.statement: Let Y be a diamond. Then the functor λ_Y^* : Y_qproét^∼ → Y_v^∼ commutes with all small limits. Similarly, if f : Y′ → Y is any map of diamonds, then f^* : Y_qproét^∼ → Y′_qproét^∼ commutes with all small limits.
items.note: C0: 'Prove 14.4–14.11: the limit-preservation assertions …'. DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Proof reduces to strictly totally disconnected X and uses the coherent sites X_qproét,qc,sep and X_v,qcqs and Lemma 14.5.

items.name: Lemma 14.5 (main part): the universal separated pro-étale quotient λ_X∘(X′)
items.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space, and X′ → X a map from a qcqs perfectoid space X′. Then there is a quasicompact separated pro-étale morphism λ_X∘(X′) → X with a factorization X′ → λ_X∘(X′) → X such that any map from X′ to a separated pro-étale perfectoid space over X factors uniquely over λ_X∘(X′).
items.note: Part of C0 ('Prove 14.4–14.11'). DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Construction via Corollary 7.22: λ_X∘(X′) corresponds to the image T of |X′| → |X| ×_{π₀X} π₀X′ (classification of qc separated pro-étale objects is D1).

items.name: Lemma 14.5(i): X′ → λ_X∘(X′) is surjective
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 14.5, the map X′ → λ_X∘(X′) is surjective. In particular, if X′₂ → X′₁ is a surjection of quasicompact separated perfectoid spaces over X, then λ_X∘(X′₂) → λ_X∘(X′₁) is surjective as well.
items.note: C0 (14.4–14.11). DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Lemma 14.5(ii): λ_X∘ commutes with fibre products of strictly totally disconnected spaces
items.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space. If X′₁ → X′₃ ← X′₂ is a diagram of strictly totally disconnected perfectoid spaces over X, then λ_X∘(X′₁ ×_{X′₃} X′₂) → λ_X∘(X′₁) ×_{λ_X∘(X′₃)} λ_X∘(X′₂) is an isomorphism.
items.note: C0 (14.4–14.11); DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. The connectedness input is Lemma 14.6, node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/geometric-connectedness-of-perfectoid-base-change (which cites 'proof of Lemma 14.5(ii)'); surjectivity step matches ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/surjectivity-criterion-for-field-pair-extensions.

items.name: Lemma 14.6: connected affinoid perfectoids stay connected under extension of geometric points
items.statement: Let X = Spa(C, C⁺), where C is an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field with an open and bounded valuation subring C⁺ ⊂ C, and let Z → X be a connected affinoid perfectoid space over X. Let X′ = Spa(C′, C′⁺) → X, where C′ is another algebraically closed nonarchimedean field with an open and bounded valuation subring C′⁺ ⊂ C′. Then Z′ := Z ×_X X′ is connected.
items.note: Node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/geometric-connectedness-of-perfectoid-base-change states it (H2: 'Also supply geometric-connectedness invariance … used in ECD Lemma 14.6'); sub-steps ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/connectedness-via-maximal-generalisations and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/geometric-connectedness-of-finite-type-spaces.

items.name: Proof of Lemma 14.4: λ_X^*F on strictly totally disconnected objects
items.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space and F a sheaf on X_qproét,qc,sep (≃ X_qproét). Then λ_X^*F on X_v,qcqs is the sheafification of the separated presheaf X′ ↦ F(λ_X∘(X′)), and for strictly totally disconnected X′ ∈ X_v,qcqs one has (λ_X^*F)(X′) = F(λ_X∘(X′)).
items.note: Key formula reused in the proofs of Proposition 14.7 and Theorem 14.12 ('by the proof of Lemma 14.4'). Part of C0. DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. See source issue: the site is misprinted X_qproét,ét,sep.

items.name: Proposition 14.7 (first part): λ_Y^* is fully faithful
items.statement: Let Y be a diamond. The functor λ_Y^* : Y_qproét^∼ → Y_v^∼ is fully faithful. Moreover, for any small sheaf F on Y_qproét, the adjunction map F → λ_{Y*}λ_Y^*F is an isomorphism.
items.note: C0: 'fully faithful pullbacks'. DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Proposition 14.7 (second part): vanishing of R^iλ_{Y*}λ_Y^*F for étale F
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond and F a sheaf of abelian groups (resp. groups) on Y_qproét that comes via pullback from Y_ét. Then R^iλ_{Y*}λ_Y^*F = 0 for all i > 0 (resp. for i = 1).
items.note: C0: 'vanishing of higher direct images for sheaves pulled back from the étale site … The vanishing in 14.7 is not claimed for all quasi-pro-étale sheaves. Its proof uses H2's geometric connectedness result and the section lemma for balls, whose ownership is D3.' DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. The source says it is unknown whether this holds for all pro-étale sheaves. See source issue: the Čech-spectral-sequence step of the proof is not justified for i ≥ 2.

items.name: Proposition 14.8: ν_Y^* is fully faithful with vanishing higher direct images
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond. The functor ν_Y^* : Y_ét^∼ → Y_qproét^∼ is fully faithful. Moreover, for any sheaf F on Y_ét, the adjunction map F → ν_{Y*}ν_Y^*F is an isomorphism, and if F is a sheaf of abelian groups (resp. groups), then R^iν_{Y*}ν_Y^*F = 0 for all i > 0 (resp. for i = 1).
items.note: C0 (14.4–14.11). DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Proof: Y_ét,qc,sep is a basis (Corollary 11.28), Pro(Y_ét,qc,sep) → Y_qproét is fully faithful with image a basis (Propositions 11.23(iii), 11.24), then as in Proposition 8.5.

items.name: Proposition 14.9: étale cohomology commutes with cofiltered limits of spatial diamonds
items.statement: Let Y_i, i ∈ I, be a cofiltered inverse system of spatial diamonds with inverse limit Y. Assume that I has a final object 0 ∈ I, and let F₀ be an étale sheaf on Y₀, with pullbacks F_i to Y_i and F to Y. Then the natural map colim_{i∈I} H^j(Y_i, F_i) → H^j(Y, F) is an isomorphism for j = 0, resp. j = 0, 1, resp. all j ≥ 0, if F₀ is a sheaf of sets, resp. a sheaf of groups, resp. a sheaf of abelian groups.
items.note: C0: 'continuity of étale cohomology'. DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Proof: Y_ét^∼ is the limit of the coherent fibred topos (Y_i)_ét,qc,sep^∼ (Proposition 11.23(iii)) and SGA 4 VI.8.7.7. The adic-space analogue is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity (not the diamond statement).

items.name: Derived categories D(T, Λ), D^±, D^b and D(Y_qproét, Λ), D(Y_v, Λ) via cutoffs
items.statement: Fix a ring Λ. For a topos T, D(T, Λ) is the derived category of Λ-modules on T, and D⁺(T, Λ), D⁻(T, Λ), D^b(T, Λ) ⊂ D(T, Λ) are the full subcategories of (cohomologically) bounded below, above, and bounded complexes. Since Y_qproét and Y_v are not generated by a set, D(Y_qproét, Λ) and D(Y_v, Λ) are defined as the filtered colimits over the choices of κ (as in Lemma 4.1) of D(Y_qproét,κ, Λ), resp. D(Y_v,κ, Λ); the transition functors are fully faithful.
items.note: C0 (bounded comparison) and C2 ('Work in an adequate cutoff D(Y_v,κ,Λ) as in 17.1'). DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Library layer for the ordinary part: mathlib:DerivedCategory (no cutoff colimit construction).

items.name: Proposition 14.10 (bounded below): D⁺(Y_ét) embeds fully faithfully
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond. Then the pullback functors ν_Y^* : D⁺(Y_ét, Λ) → D⁺(Y_qproét, Λ) and λ_Y^*ν_Y^* : D⁺(Y_ét, Λ) → D⁺(Y_v, Λ) are fully faithful.
items.note: C0: 'the bounded-below derived comparisons'. DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Follows from Propositions 14.7 and 14.8.

items.name: Proposition 14.10 (unbounded, strictly totally disconnected Y)
items.statement: If Y is a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space, then the pullback functors ν_Y^* : D(Y_ét, Λ) → D(Y_qproét, Λ) and λ_Y^*ν_Y^* : D(Y_ét, Λ) → D(Y_v, Λ) are fully faithful.
items.note: C0: 'Prove the unbounded comparison for strictly totally disconnected spaces.' DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Uses left-completeness (Proposition 14.11).

items.name: Proposition 14.11: left-completeness of D(Y_v), D(Y_qproét), D(Y_ét)
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack. (i) The derived category D(Y_v, Λ) is left-complete. (ii) If Y is a diamond, then D(Y_qproét, Λ) is left-complete. (iii) If Y is a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space, then D(Y_ét, Λ) is left-complete.
items.note: Proved in the proof of Proposition 14.10 (bases of objects with vanishing higher cohomology: strictly w-local U with extremally disconnected π₀U for Y_qproét, strictly totally disconnected U for Y_ét; Y_v is replete, [BS15, Proposition 3.3.3]). C0: 'Verify repleteness and left-completeness for the actual v-sites and quasi-pro-étale sites … apply E2'. Nodes EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/left-completion, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/replete-topoi. DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Theorem 14.12: being étale can be checked v-locally
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond and f : Y′ → Y a v-cover by a locally spatial diamond Y′. (i) If A ∈ D(Y_qproét, Λ) or A ∈ D(Y_v, Λ) and f^*A ∈ D⁺(Y′_ét, Λ), then A ∈ D⁺(Y_ét, Λ). (ii) If A ∈ D(Y_qproét, Λ) or A ∈ D(Y_v, Λ), Y and Y′ are strictly totally disconnected, and f^*A ∈ D(Y′_ét, Λ), then A ∈ D(Y_ét, Λ). (Here D⁺(Y_ét, Λ), D(Y_ét, Λ) are regarded as full subcategories via Proposition 14.10.)
items.note: C2: 'Now prove Theorem 14.12, using C1 exactly where its proof invokes 16.1.' DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. The proof uses Theorem 16.1 (i = 0) and the formula (λ_X^*F)(X′) = F(λ_X∘(X′)).

items.name: Definition 14.13: D_ét(Y, Λ)
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack. Define the full subcategory D_ét(Y, Λ) ⊂ D(Y, Λ) = D(Y_v, Λ) as consisting of those A ∈ D(Y, Λ) such that for all strictly totally disconnected perfectoid spaces f : X → Y, the pullback f^*A ∈ D(X_ét, Λ).
items.note: C2: 'Define D_ét as the full subcategory of the enhanced v-derived category tested on strictly totally disconnected perfectoids (14.13).' DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Remark 14.14: D_ét on one cover; comparison with D(Y_ét)
items.statement: By Theorem 14.12, it suffices to check the condition of Definition 14.13 for one v-cover of Y. If Y is a locally spatial diamond, D⁺_ét(Y, Λ) = D⁺(Y_ét, Λ), and if Y is a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space, D_ét(Y, Λ) = D(Y_ét, Λ). If Y is a locally spatial diamond, in general D_ét(Y, Λ) ≠ D(Y_ét, Λ).
items.note: C2: 'Prove that it can be tested on one v-cover'. DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Proposition 14.15 (first part): D_ét(Y, Λ) is left-complete
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack. Then D_ét(Y, Λ) is left-complete.
items.note: 'The first part is clear.' C2 (14.15–14.16). DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Proposition 14.15 (second part): D_ét is the left completion of D(Y_ét) for locally spatial Y
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond. Then D_ét(Y, Λ) is the left-completion of D(Y_ét, Λ). In particular, the fully faithful embedding D⁺(Y_ét, Λ) ⊂ D(Y_qproét, Λ) extends to a fully faithful embedding D_ét(Y, Λ) ⊂ D(Y_qproét, Λ).
items.note: C2: 'the identification with the left completion of the ordinary étale derived category for locally spatial diamonds (14.15–14.16)'; C8 packet request to C2: 'The canonical 14.15 identification of D_et with Postnikov left completion'. Generic layer: EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/postnikov-left-completion. Proof 'the same as in [BS15, Proposition 5.3.2]'. DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Proposition 14.16: membership in D_ét is detected on cohomology sheaves
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack and A ∈ D(Y, Λ). Then A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ) if and only if for all i ∈ ℤ, the v-sheaf Hⁱ(A)[0] ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ).
items.note: C2: 'the cohomology-sheaf criterion'. DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: Spd ℤ_p and Spd(A, A⁺) (marked untilts; stated in Lemma 15.1)
items.statement: Spd ℤ_p is the functor on Perf taking X to the set of pairs (X♯, ι) up to isomorphism, where X♯ is a perfectoid space and ι : (X♯)♭ ≅ X identifies X♯ as an untilt of X. For a Tate ℤ_p-algebra A and an open and integrally closed subring A⁺ ⊂ A, Spd(A, A⁺) takes X ∈ Perf to the set of pairs ((X♯, ι), f : (A, A⁺) → (O_{X♯}(X♯), O⁺_{X♯}(X♯))) up to isomorphism, with (X♯, ι) as before and f a continuous map of pairs of topological algebras. Functoriality in X uses Corollary 3.20 (perfectoid spaces over X ≃ perfectoid spaces over X♯), and pairs (X♯, ι) have no automorphisms.
items.locator: Lemma 15.1 and first paragraph of its proof, p. 89, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair states both functors. D6: 'Construct Spd ℤ_p by marked untilts, proving functorial pullback from the tilting equivalence, absence of automorphisms, and v-descent. Construct Spd(A,A⁺) for a Tate ℤ_p-pair'.

items.name: Lemma 15.1(i): Spd ℤ_p is a v-sheaf
items.statement: The functor Spd ℤ_p taking X ∈ Perf to the set of pairs (X♯, ι) up to isomorphism, where X♯ is a perfectoid space and ι : (X♯)♭ ≅ X is an identification of X♯ as an untilt of X, is a v-sheaf.
items.note: Nodes DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair and DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers (descent of untilts along a v-cover Y → X of affinoid perfectoids, via Fontaine's θ, Theorem 8.7 and R♯ = (W(R⁺)/ξ)[1/[ϖ]]).

items.name: Lemma 15.1(ii): Spd(A, A⁺) is a v-sheaf
items.statement: Let A be a Tate ℤ_p-algebra, and let A⁺ ⊂ A be an open and integrally closed subring. The functor Spd(A, A⁺) taking X ∈ Perf to the set of pairs ((X♯, ι), f : (A, A⁺) → (O_{X♯}(X♯), O⁺_{X♯}(X♯))) up to isomorphism, where (X♯, ι) is as in (i) and f is a continuous map of pairs of topological algebras, is a v-sheaf.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair. Follows from (i) and Theorem 8.7.

items.name: Lemma 15.2: Spd of a perfectoid Tate pair is its tilt
items.statement: Let A be a perfectoid Tate ring with an open and integrally closed subring A⁺ ⊂ A. Then Spd(A, A⁺) is representable by the affinoid perfectoid space Spa(A♭, A♭⁺).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair (locator 'Lemma 15.2 with proof'). D6: 'a perfectoid pair gives its tilt'. Direct consequence of Corollary 3.20.

items.name: Lemma 15.3 (first part): finite étale torsor tower killing all finite étale covers
items.statement: Let A be any ring. Then one can find a cofiltered inverse system of finite groups G_i with surjective transition maps, and a compatible filtered direct system of finite étale G_i-torsors A → A_i such that A_∞ = colim_i A_i has no nonsplit finite étale covers.
items.note: Node AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower ('ECD Lemma 15.3, first part'), with AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-split-ring, AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-galois-torsor, AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/splitting-torsor-of-finite-etale-algebra. 'The first part is standard' in the source.

items.name: Lemma 15.3 (second part): the uniform completion of A_∞ is perfectoid
items.statement: In the situation of the first part, if A is a Tate ℤ_p-algebra, then the uniform completion Â_∞ of A_∞ is perfectoid.
items.note: Node AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-uniform-completion ('ECD Lemma 15.3, second part') with sub-steps AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/pseudouniformizer-dividing-p, AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/frobenius-surjective-for-split-tate-ring, AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/root-of-monic-in-split-tate-ring. The atlas plans it only for complete A: the statement as printed is false for non-complete Tate rings (source issue AdicEtaleGeometry/E19) and the Frobenius step has a gap (AdicEtaleGeometry/E20). Results of this type are due to Colmez [Col02] and Faltings [Fal02].

items.name: Proposition 15.4 (first part): Spd(A, A⁺) is a spatial diamond via a perfectoid G-torsor
items.statement: Let A be a Tate ℤ_p-algebra with an open and integrally closed subring A⁺ ⊂ A, and choose G_i and A → A_i as in Lemma 15.3. Let A_i⁺ ⊂ A_i be the integral closure of A⁺, and let Â_∞⁺ ⊂ Â_∞ be the closure of colim_i A_i⁺ in Â_∞. Then Spd(A_i, A_i⁺) → Spd(A, A⁺) is a G_i-torsor of v-sheaves, and Spd(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) = lim_i Spd(A_i, A_i⁺) → Spd(A, A⁺) is a G-torsor, where G = lim_i G_i. In particular Spa(Â_∞^♭, Â_∞^{♭+}) = Spd(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) → Spd(A, A⁺) is a universally open qcqs quasi-pro-étale map from an affinoid perfectoid space, so that Spd(A, A⁺) is a spatial diamond.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond states it; analytic inputs AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-cover-presentation and AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/spd-of-tate-huber-pair-and-perfectoid-torsor (A4 part only for complete A). Proof: Theorem 6.1, Lemmas 15.2, 15.3, 10.13, Proposition 11.24; inherits source issue AdicEtaleGeometry/E19 for non-complete A (replace A by its completion).

items.name: Proposition 15.4 (second part): |Spd(A, A⁺)| = |Spa(A, A⁺)|
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 15.4, |Spd(A, A⁺)| = |Spa(Â_∞^♭, Â_∞^{♭+})|/G = |Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)|/G = |Spa(A, A⁺)|.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond; the topological input |Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺)| = lim_i |Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)| and |Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)|/G_i = |Spa(A, A⁺)| is node AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/spa-of-completed-tower (with AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/torsor-spa-orbits).

items.name: Rational opens give open subfunctors of Spd(A, A⁺)
items.statement: If U ⊂ Spa(A, A⁺) is a rational open subset, then Spd(O(U), O⁺(U)) → Spd(A, A⁺) is the open subfunctor of Spd(A, A⁺) corresponding to the open subset U ⊂ |Spa(A, A⁺)| = |Spd(A, A⁺)|; hence (A, A⁺) ↦ Spd(A, A⁺) glues to analytic adic spaces.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor states it. No proof is given in the source.

items.name: Definition 15.5: the diamond Y^♢ of an analytic adic space over ℤ_p
items.statement: Let Y be an analytic adic space over ℤ_p. The diamond associated with Y is the v-sheaf Y^♢ : X ↦ {((X♯, ι), f : X♯ → Y)}/≅, where X♯ is a perfectoid space with an isomorphism ι : (X♯)♭ ≅ X. (The definition and Lemma 15.6 work for adic spaces in the generality of [SW13, Section 2.1].)
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor; generalized adic spaces are AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation.

items.name: Lemma 15.6 (first part): Y^♢ is a locally spatial diamond with |Y^♢| = |Y|
items.statement: Let Y be an analytic adic space over ℤ_p. Then Y^♢ is a locally spatial diamond, with |Y^♢| = |Y|.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison; affinoid case is Proposition 15.4. A4 boundary node AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/diamond-of-analytic-adic-space-and-etale-site-15-6.

items.name: Lemma 15.6 (second part): finite étale sites agree
items.statement: Let Y be an analytic adic space over ℤ_p. With Y_fét defined as in [KL15, Definition 8.2.19], one has an equivalence of sites Y^♢_fét ≅ Y_fét.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison. Inputs: [KL15, Lemma 8.2.17] (node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized), [Sch12, Lemma 7.5(i)] and descent along the torsor tower (nodes AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-invariance-along-tower, AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-effective-descent-along-tower, AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-self-product).

items.name: Lemma 15.6 (third part): étale sites agree
items.statement: Let Y be an analytic adic space over ℤ_p. With Y_ét defined as in [KL15, Definition 8.2.19], one has an equivalence of sites Y^♢_ét ≅ Y_ét.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison. Proof combines |Y^♢| = |Y| with the finite étale case, since by Lemma 11.31 resp. [KL15, Definition 8.2.16] étale maps are locally a quasicompact open immersion followed by a finite étale map (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized).

items.name: Theorem 16.1(i): v- vs pro-étale pushforward, degree 0
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of locally spatial diamonds, with the commutative square of sites λ_{Y′} : Y′_v → Y′_qproét, λ_Y : Y_v → Y_qproét, f_v : Y′_v → Y_v, f_qproét : Y′_qproét → Y_qproét. Let F be a small sheaf of abelian groups on Y′_qproét that comes via pullback from Y′_ét. Then the base change morphism λ_Y^* R^i f_qproét* F → R^i f_v* λ_{Y′}^* F is an isomorphism for i = 0. Moreover, under the same condition, if Y = X and X̃ ∈ X_v are strictly totally disconnected and X̃ → λ_X∘(X̃) → X is the factorization from Lemma 14.5, then the natural map Hⁱ((λ_X∘(X̃) ×_X Y′)_qproét, F) → Hⁱ((X̃ ×_X Y′)_v, λ_{Y′}^*F) is an isomorphism.
items.note: C1: 'Prove ECD Theorem 16.1 and its corollaries using D6's analytic comparison, H2's valued-field invariance, and C0. Retain its separate cases: degree zero, the quasi-pro-étale case, and the prime-to-p torsion-cohomology case.' DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Degree-0 case uses Lemma 14.6. Remark 16.2: for geometric points X, X̃ this says Hⁱ(Y′_qproét, F) = Hⁱ(Y′_v, λ^*F) = Hⁱ((X̃ ×_X Y′)_v, λ^*F).

items.name: Theorem 16.1(ii): v- vs pro-étale pushforward for quasi-pro-étale f
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of locally spatial diamonds, with the commutative square of sites λ_{Y′} : Y′_v → Y′_qproét, λ_Y : Y_v → Y_qproét, f_v : Y′_v → Y_v, f_qproét : Y′_qproét → Y_qproét. Let F be a small sheaf of abelian groups on Y′_qproét that comes via pullback from Y′_ét. Then the base change morphism λ_Y^* R^i f_qproét* F → R^i f_v* λ_{Y′}^* F is an isomorphism for all i ≥ 0 if f is quasi-pro-étale. Moreover, under the same condition, if Y = X and X̃ ∈ X_v are strictly totally disconnected and X̃ → λ_X∘(X̃) → X is the factorization from Lemma 14.5, then the natural map Hⁱ((λ_X∘(X̃) ×_X Y′)_qproét, F) → Hⁱ((X̃ ×_X Y′)_v, λ_{Y′}^*F) is an isomorphism.
items.note: C1: 'Prove ECD Theorem 16.1 and its corollaries using D6's analytic comparison, H2's valued-field invariance, and C0. items.name: Theorem 16.1(iii): v- vs pro-étale pushforward for prime-to-p torsion
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of locally spatial diamonds, with the commutative square of sites λ_{Y′} : Y′_v → Y′_qproét, λ_Y : Y_v → Y_qproét, f_v : Y′_v → Y_v, f_qproét : Y′_qproét → Y_qproét. Let F be a small sheaf of abelian groups on Y′_qproét that comes via pullback from Y′_ét. Then the base change morphism λ_Y^* R^i f_qproét* F → R^i f_v* λ_{Y′}^* F is an isomorphism for all i ≥ 0 if there is some integer n prime to p such that nF = 0. Moreover, under the same condition, if Y = X and X̃ ∈ X_v are strictly totally disconnected and X̃ → λ_X∘(X̃) → X is the factorization from Lemma 14.5, then the natural map Hⁱ((λ_X∘(X̃) ×_X Y′)_qproét, F) → Hⁱ((X̃ ×_X Y′)_v, λ_{Y′}^*F) is an isomorphism.

DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Reduces to F = j_!M on a local space and Lemma 16.3; node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/extension-by-zero-over-geometric-field-pairs cites 'proof of Theorem 16.1'.

items.name: Lemma 16.3: prime-to-p cohomology of j_!M on X₁ ×_{X₃} X₂ for geometric points
items.statement: Let X_i = Spa(C_i, C_i⁺) for i = 1, 2, 3, where C_i is an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field with an open and bounded valuation subring C_i⁺ ⊂ C_i, and let X₁ → X₃ ← X₂ be a diagram, with X₁ → X₃ surjective. Let j₂ : U₂ ↪ X₂ be a quasicompact open subset and M an abelian group killed by some n prime to p. Then Hⁱ((X₁ ×_{X₃} X₂)_ét, j₂!M) = 0 for all i ≥ 0 unless U₂ = X₂ and i = 0, in which case one gets M.
items.note: Node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/extension-by-zero-over-geometric-field-pairs ('ECD Lemma 16.3'), via ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/invariance-for-perfectoid-affinoids, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/invariance-for-affinoids-of-finite-type ([Hub96, Theorem 4.1.1(c)]) and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/finite-type-approximation-of-perfectoid-affinoids. Proof also uses Proposition 14.9 and Lemma 15.6. Source issues ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology/E6, E7 already recorded.

items.name: Corollary 16.4: derived v- vs pro-étale base change for D_ét
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of locally spatial diamonds. Assume that f is quasi-pro-étale, or nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Then for any A ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ) ⊂ D(Y′_qproét, Λ), the base change morphism λ_Y^* Rf_qproét* A → Rf_v* λ_{Y′}^* A in D(Y_v, Λ) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Corollary 16.5: Rf_v* A is étale when Rf_qproét* A is
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of locally spatial diamonds. Assume that f is quasi-pro-étale, or nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. If A ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ) is such that Rf_qproét* A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ) ⊂ D(Y_qproét, Λ), then the pushforward Rf_v* A lies in D_ét(Y, Λ) ⊂ D(Y, Λ) and agrees with Rf_qproét* A.

items.name: Proposition 16.6: étale vs pro-étale pushforward for qcqs maps

items.name: Corollary 16.7 (unbounded, strictly totally disconnected Y, Y′)
items.statement: If Y and Y′ are strictly totally disconnected perfectoid spaces and f : Y′ → Y is qcqs, then for any A ∈ D(Y′_ét, Λ) the base change morphism ν_Y^* Rf_ét* A → Rf_qproét* ν_{Y′}^* A is an isomorphism.

items.name: Corollary 16.8(i): Rf_v* preserves D_ét for qcqs quasi-pro-étale f
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a qcqs map of small v-stacks. If f is quasi-pro-étale, then for any A ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ), the pushforward Rf_v* A lies in D_ét(Y, Λ).
items.note: C1 (corollaries of 16.1). DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Proof: reduce to Y strictly totally disconnected; separated Y′ is strictly totally disconnected (Lemma 7.19); general Y′ by a finite Čech cover; Corollaries 16.7 and 16.5.

items.name: Corollary 16.8(ii): Rf_v* preserves D⁺_ét for prime-to-p torsion Λ and agrees with Rf_ét*
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a qcqs map of small v-stacks and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Then for any A ∈ D⁺_ét(Y′, Λ), the pushforward Rf_v* A lies in D⁺_ét(Y, Λ). If Y and Y′ are locally spatial, then under the identifications D⁺_ét(Y′, Λ) = D⁺(Y′_ét, Λ) and D⁺_ét(Y, Λ) = D⁺(Y_ét, Λ), one has Rf_v* = Rf_ét*.

items.name: Corollary 16.9 (sheaves): pro-étale base change in cartesian squares
items.statement: Let Y′ →(g′) Y, f′ : Y′ → X′, f : Y → X, g : X′ → X form a cartesian diagram of locally spatial diamonds, and let F be a small sheaf of abelian groups on Y_qproét that comes via pullback from Y_ét. Then the base change morphism g^*_qproét R^i f_qproét* F → R^i f′_qproét* g′^*_qproét F is an isomorphism in the following cases: (i) if i = 0; (ii) for all i ≥ 0 if f or g is quasi-pro-étale; (iii) for all i ≥ 0 if nF = 0 for some n prime to p.

items.name: Lemma 17.1: D_ét(Y, Λ) is a presentable stable ∞-category
items.statement: For a small v-stack Y there is a (natural) presentable stable ∞-category 𝒟_ét(Y, Λ) whose homotopy category is D_ét(Y, Λ). More precisely, for each sufficiently large κ as in Lemma 4.1, the ∞-derived category 𝒟(Y_v,κ, Λ) of Λ-modules on Y_v,κ is a presentable stable ∞-category, and for κ large enough, 𝒟_ét(Y, Λ) is a full presentable stable ∞-subcategory closed under all colimits.

DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. items.name: Corollary 17.2: the étale coreflection R_Yét
items.statement: For any small v-stack Y, the inclusion D_ét(Y, Λ) ⊂ D(Y_v, Λ) has a right adjoint R_Yét : D(Y_v, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ).

Proof: [Lur09, Corollary 5.5.2.9] at each cutoff κ.

items.name: Formula for R_Yét on D⁺ (stated after Corollary 17.2)
items.statement: If Y is a locally spatial diamond, then on D⁺(Y_v, Λ) the right adjoint R_Yét is given by R(ν∘λ)_*, where ν∘λ : Y_v → Y_ét is the map of sites; for strictly totally disconnected Y this formula holds on all of D(Y_v, Λ).

items.name: Proposition 17.3: hyperdescent for D(Y_v, Λ)
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack, and let Y_• → Y be a simplicial v-hypercover of Y by small v-stacks Y_• with 0-truncated maps Y_i → Y. Let 𝒟(Y_•,v, Λ) be the ∞-derived category of sheaves of Λ-modules on the simplicial site Y_•,v, with homotopy category D(Y_•,v, Λ). Pullback along Y_• → Y induces a fully faithful functor 𝒟(Y_v, Λ) → 𝒟(Y_•,v, Λ) whose essential image is the full ∞-subcategory of cartesian objects; in particular D(Y_v, Λ) → D(Y_•,v, Λ) is fully faithful with essential image the cartesian objects.
items.note: C2: 'Prove presentability and stability with the size bounds and generating/localization argument of 17.1 … Construct compatible right adjoints at the cutoffs to obtain the right adjoint to the inclusion (17.2), and enhanced hyperdescent (17.3).' DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Generic layer: EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/unbounded-hypercover-descent, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/hypercovers-and-cohomological-descent. Proof cites [Sta, Tag 0DC7] and [BS15, Proposition 3.3.6].

items.name: Remark 17.4: D_ét(Y, Λ) lies in one cutoff
items.statement: Choosing a simplicial v-hypercover Y_• → Y by disjoint unions of strictly totally disconnected spaces, and using that D_ét(Y_i, Λ) = D(Y_i,ét, Λ) is contained in D(Y_i,v,κ, Λ) for any κ such that Y_i is κ-small, one has D_ét(Y, Λ) = D_ét,cart(Y_•, Λ), which is therefore contained in D(Y_v,κ, Λ) for such κ.
items.note: C2: 'Prove presentability and stability with the size bounds and generating/localization argument of 17.1 … Construct compatible right adjoints at the cutoffs to obtain the right adjoint to the inclusion (17.2), and enhanced hyperdescent (17.3).' items.name: Pullback f^* on D(Y_v, Λ) and D_ét for arbitrary maps of small v-stacks
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of small v-stacks. If f is 0-truncated, f induces a map of sites f_v : Y′_v → Y_v and a functor of ∞-categories f_v^* : 𝒟(Y_v, Λ) → 𝒟(Y′_v, Λ). In general, choose a perfectoid space Y′₀ with a surjective map of v-stacks Y′₀ → Y′ and let Y′_• be its Čech nerve (small v-sheaves; all Y′_i → Y′ and Y′_i → Y are 0-truncated); pullback gives f_v^* : 𝒟(Y_v, Λ) → 𝒟_cart(Y′_•,v, Λ) ≃ 𝒟(Y′_v, Λ), which carries 𝒟_ét into 𝒟_ét and gives f^* : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ). This is canonically independent of the choices and compatible with composition: for g : Y″ → Y′, (f∘g)^* ≃ g^*∘f^* with the usual coherences.
items.locator: paragraphs before and after Proposition 17.3, pp. 97–98, arXiv:1709.07343v4

Prove the adjunctions, functoriality, identity and composition laws … Prove all the tensor/Hom identities of §17.' items.name: Lemma 17.5: Rf_* exists on D_ét
items.statement: For any map of small v-stacks f : Y′ → Y, the functor f^* : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ) has a right adjoint Rf_* : D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ).

items.name: Proposition 17.6 (bounded below): Rf_* = Rf_v* and base change, prime-to-p torsion
items.statement: Assume that nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let f : Y′ → Y be a qcqs map of small v-stacks. Then for any A ∈ D⁺_ét(Y′, Λ), one has Rf_v* A ∈ D⁺_ét(Y, Λ), and thus Rf_* A = Rf_v* A. Moreover, in this case the formation of Rf_* commutes with any base change: for all maps g : Ỹ → Y of small v-stacks with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ, g′ : Ỹ′ → Y′, the natural transformation g^* Rf_* A → Rf̃_* g′^* A is an equivalence for all A ∈ D⁺_ét(Y′, Λ).

items.name: Proposition 17.6 (finite cohomological dimension): unbounded Rf_* = Rf_v* and base change
items.statement: Assume that nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p and let f : Y′ → Y be a qcqs map of small v-stacks. If Rf_* has finite cohomological dimension, i.e. there is an integer N such that for all A ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ) concentrated in degree 0, R^i f_* A = 0 for i > N, then for all A ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ) one has Rf_* A = Rf_v* A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ), and for every map g : Ỹ → Y of small v-stacks the base change morphism g^* Rf_* A → Rf̃_* g′^* A is an isomorphism. (Only Rf_*, not Rf̃_*, needs finite cohomological dimension.)

items.name: Derived tensor product on D(Y_v, Λ) and its compatibility with f^*
items.statement: For a small v-stack Y there is a natural functor − ⊗^L_Λ − : D(Y_v, Λ) × D(Y_v, Λ) → D(Y_v, Λ), as for any ringed topos, already defined as a functor of ∞-categories 𝒟(Y_v, Λ) × 𝒟(Y_v, Λ) → 𝒟(Y_v, Λ) preserving all colimits separately in each variable (𝒟(Y_v, Λ) is presentably symmetric monoidal). If f : Y′ → Y is any map of small v-stacks, there is a natural equivalence f^*(A ⊗^L_Λ B) ≃ f^*A ⊗^L_Λ f^*B for all A, B ∈ D(Y_v, Λ).

items.name: Lemma 17.7: ⊗^L preserves D_ét; D_ét is presentably symmetric monoidal
items.statement: For any small v-stack Y, the functor − ⊗^L_Λ − : D(Y_v, Λ) × D(Y_v, Λ) → D(Y_v, Λ) induces by restriction a functor − ⊗^L_Λ − : D_ét(Y, Λ) × D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ). Consequently 𝒟_ét(Y, Λ) is a presentably symmetric monoidal ∞-category (in a unique way compatible with the standard symmetric monoidal structure on 𝒟(Y_v, Λ)).

items.name: Lemma 17.8: internal Hom on D_ét
items.statement: For any small v-stack Y and A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ), the functor D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ), B ↦ B ⊗^L_Λ A admits a right adjoint D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ), C ↦ RHom_Λ(A, C), i.e. Hom_{D_ét(Y,Λ)}(B ⊗^L_Λ A, C) = Hom_{D_ét(Y,Λ)}(B, RHom_Λ(A, C)). For varying A these assemble into a functor RHom_Λ(−, −) : D_ét(Y, Λ)^op × D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ). (In general it is not the inner Hom of D(Y_v, Λ); one must apply R_Yét to the latter.)

Prove the adjunctions, functoriality, identity and composition laws … Prove all the tensor/Hom identities of §17.' DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only. Proof uses [Lur09, Proposition 5.5.2.2].

items.name: Corollary 17.9: Rf_* RHom(f^*A, B) ≅ RHom(A, Rf_* B)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of small v-stacks. There is a natural equivalence Rf_* RHom_Λ(f^*A, B) ≅ RHom_Λ(A, Rf_* B) of functors D_ét(Y, Λ)^op × D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ).
items.note: C3: 'Construct derived tensor and f* as the allowed restrictions of v-operations; construct internal Hom and Rf* using étale coreflection where required. Prove the adjunctions, functoriality, identity and composition laws … Prove all the tensor/Hom identities of §17.' DiamondEtaleCohomology has blueprint nodes only for C8 (packet DiamondEtaleCohomology--C8.json); this is planned at stage level only.

items.name: External: [Sta, Tag 02UW] — constant coefficients on a spectral space with a generic point
items.statement: (As used) If T is a spectral space with a unique generic point (e.g. the closure in |Y| of a rank-one point) and M is an abelian group, then RΓ(T, M) = M, i.e. Hⁱ(T, M) = 0 for i > 0 and H⁰(T, M) = M.
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 13.13, p. 81, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nearest library layer: tauceti:TauCeti.Topology.subsingleton_H_succ_of_isFlasque (flasque sheaves are acyclic) and mathlib:TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque; missing the step that a constant sheaf on an irreducible space (every nonempty open contains the generic point) is flasque with global sections M. D5 plans 13.13 'using D0' but no stage or node states this lemma.

items.name: External: [Sch12, Lemma 6.13] — approximation of affinoid perfectoids by p-finite spaces
items.statement: (As used) An affinoid perfectoid space Z over (C, O_C), C algebraically closed nonarchimedean, can be written as a cofiltered inverse limit of p-finite (affinoid, topologically of finite type) spaces Z_i over (C, O_C); quasicompact open (in particular clopen) subsets of Z come from some Z_i.
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemma 14.6, p. 84, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/finite-type-approximation-of-perfectoid-affinoids (H2: 'Establish approximation of perfectoid affinoids by the p-finite analytic spaces used in Sch12').

items.name: External: geometric connectedness of rigid spaces is invariant under algebraically closed base extension
items.statement: (As used) For rigid spaces (adic spaces of finite type) over an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C, connectedness is preserved by base change to an algebraically closed complete extension C′ ⊃ C.
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemma 14.6, p. 84, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/geometric-connectedness-of-finite-type-spaces.

items.name: External: SGA 4 VI.8.7.7 — cohomology of a limit of coherent topoi
items.statement: (As used) For a cofiltered system of coherent topoi with coherent transition morphisms, and an abelian sheaf pulled back from one stage, the cohomology of the limit topos is the filtered colimit of the cohomologies of the stages (with the analogous statements in degree 0 for sheaves of sets and degrees 0, 1 for sheaves of groups).
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 14.9, p. 86, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Not stated by any stage or node for general coherent topoi. C0 plans the conclusion (Proposition 14.9, 'continuity of étale cohomology'); ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity is the analogue for adic spaces (Huber 2.4.6); DiamondsAndVStacks:D0 builds coherent/algebraic topos interfaces but not limits of topoi.

items.name: External: [BS15, Proposition 3.3.3] — replete topoi have left-complete derived categories
items.statement: (As used) If T is a replete topos, then D(T, Λ) is left-complete: A ≅ R lim_n τ^{≥−n}A for all A.
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 14.10 and in Proposition 14.11(i), p. 86, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/left-completion ('If X is a replete topos, Ψ : D(X) → D̂(X) is an equivalence with inverse Rlim'); repleteness of Y_v is to be verified in C0.

items.name: External: [BS15, Proposition 5.3.2] — left completion of the étale derived category
items.statement: (As used) The argument identifying the left completion of D(X_ét, Λ) with the full subcategory of the (left-complete) pro-étale derived category of objects whose cohomology sheaves come from the étale site.
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 14.15, p. 88, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: C2 plans 14.15 ('identification with the left completion of the ordinary étale derived category'); generic layer EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/postnikov-left-completion.

items.name: External: [BS15, Proposition 3.1.11] — R lim has cohomological dimension ≤ 1 in a replete topos
items.statement: (As used) In a replete topos, R lim_n of an inverse sequence of sheaves has cohomology only in degrees 0 and 1.
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 17.6, p. 99, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/inverse-limit-amplitude states exactly this.

items.name: External: [Sta, Tag 0DC7], [BS15, Proposition 3.3.6] — cohomological descent along hypercovers
items.statement: (As used) For a hypercover U_• of a site, pullback identifies the derived category of the site with the full subcategory of cartesian objects in the derived category of the simplicial site.
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 17.3, p. 97, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Nodes EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/unbounded-hypercover-descent (replete case) and EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/hypercovers-and-cohomological-descent.

items.name: External: [Hub96, Theorem 4.1.1(c)] — invariance under extension of algebraically closed fields
items.statement: (As used) For an affinoid adic space Spa(R, R⁺) topologically of finite type over (C₃, C₃⁺), a surjective extension of algebraically closed fields with open bounded valuation subrings, a quasicompact open U, and M killed by n prime to p, étale cohomology of j_!M is unchanged by the base extension.
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemma 16.3, p. 93, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/invariance-for-affinoids-of-finite-type ('Hub96 4.1.1(c) in the form of ECD Lemma 16.3').

items.name: External: [KL15, Definitions 8.2.16, 8.2.19, Lemma 8.2.17] — étale and finite étale sites of analytic adic spaces
items.statement: (As used) Étale and finite étale morphisms of (generalized) analytic adic spaces defined locally by open immersions and finite étale maps, the sites Y_ét and Y_fét, and for a Tate pair (A, A⁺) the equivalence of finite étale A-algebras with (Spa(A, A⁺)_fét)^op.
items.locator: used in Lemma 15.6 and its proof, p. 91, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.19, Lemma 8.2.17), with AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism (Definition 8.2.16).

items.name: External: [Sch12, Lemma 7.5(i)] — finite étale algebras over a completed colimit
items.statement: (As used) (Â_∞)_fét = 2-colim_i (A_i)_fét for the completed colimit of the torsor tower; similarly for C⁰(G, Â_∞) and C⁰(G × G, Â_∞).
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemma 15.6, p. 91, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-invariance-along-tower states (i)–(ii) for complete (A, A⁺).

items.name: External: [Lur09, Corollary 5.5.2.9] — adjoint functor theorem for presentable ∞-categories
items.statement: (As used) A colimit-preserving functor between presentable ∞-categories admits a right adjoint.
items.locator: used in the proofs of Corollary 17.2 and Lemma 17.5, pp. 97–98, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/adjoint-functor-theorem-and-localisations. Mathlib has only 1-categorical adjoint functor theorems (e.g. CategoryTheory.isRightAdjoint_of_preservesLimits_of_isCoseparating), which do not give the ∞-categorical statement.

items.name: External: [Lur09, Proposition 5.5.2.2] — representability on presentable ∞-categories
items.statement: (As used) For a presentable ∞-category C, a functor C^op → S (spaces) is representable if and only if it preserves small limits.
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemma 17.8, p. 100, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Not stated by any stage or node. Nearest: EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/adjoint-functor-theorem-and-localisations (adjoint functor theorem, of which this is the core) and EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:presentability/presentable-categories.

items.name: External: [Lur09, Proposition 5.5.3.12] — limits of presentable ∞-categories
items.statement: (As used) A limit of presentable ∞-categories along colimit-preserving functors is presentable (computed in ∞-categories), so presentability of 𝒟_ét(Y, Λ) can be checked on a hypercover.
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemma 17.1, p. 96, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Not stated by any stage or node. Nearest: EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:presentability/presentable-categories (definition only) and E3's accessible localizations; C2 plans Lemma 17.1 itself.

items.name: External: Fontaine's map θ : W(S⁺) → S♯⁺
items.statement: (As used) For an untilt S♯ of a perfectoid S with S⁺ = (S♯⁺)♭, Fontaine's ring homomorphism θ : W(S⁺) → S♯⁺ with θ([x]) = x♯.
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemma 15.1, p. 89, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Checked: mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta : 𝕎 (PreTilt R p) →+* R (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean) for p-adically complete R with p not a unit, with fontaineTheta_teichmuller (θ([x]) is the untilt of x) and surjective_fontaineTheta. Identifying S⁺ with PreTilt(S♯⁺) is the tilting equivalence (§3, outside this range).

items.name: Definition 18.1: proper map of v-stacks
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of v-stacks. f is proper if it is quasicompact, separated and universally closed, i.e. for every small v-sheaf X with a map X → Y the map |Y′ ×_Y X| → |X| is closed. (As f is quasicompact, Y′ ×_Y X is a small v-sheaf for small X; by the definition of the topology on |X| it suffices to test perfectoid X, or even strictly totally disconnected perfectoid X.)
items.note: C4 ('Build ECD §18 … define properness, prove the valuative criteria, and construct the partially proper envelope/canonical compactification with its universal property … functoriality, base-change compatibility, the affinoid formula over a strictly totally disconnected base, and the behavior of qc maps … the tautness comparison'). No blueprint packet exists for C4 yet, so there is no node id. Explicitly 'Define properness'. The nearest existing layer is Huber's notion for adic spaces, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism, but that is a different category.

items.name: Remark 18.2(a): closed immersions are proper
items.statement: Any closed immersion of v-sheaves is a proper map.
items.note: C4 plans all of §18 ('Build ECD §18') but does not name this remark separately. No packet node exists.

items.name: Remark 18.2(b): proper maps of locally compact Hausdorff spaces (exercise)
items.statement: If T′ → T is a map of locally compact Hausdorff spaces, then the induced map of associated v-sheaves T′ → T is proper (Definition 18.1) if and only if T′ → T is proper in the usual topological sense.
items.note: The source leaves this to the reader as an exercise and gives no proof, and nothing later in the range uses it. No stage names it. The nearest is D4/D5's compact-Hausdorff diamond tests (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4 tests the 11.12 example; D5 treats proper zero-dimensional compact-Hausdorff examples), but these do not state the properness comparison.

items.name: Proposition 18.3: valuative criterion of properness
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of v-stacks. Then f is proper if and only if f is 0-truncated, quasicompact and quasiseparated, and for every perfectoid field K with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K and every commutative square Spa(K,O_K) → Y′, Spa(K,K⁺) → Y (compatible via f), there is a unique map Spa(K,K⁺) → Y′ making the diagram commute.
items.note: C4 ('Build ECD §18 … define properness, prove the valuative criteria, and construct the partially proper envelope/canonical compactification with its universal property … functoriality, base-change compatibility, the affinoid formula over a strictly totally disconnected base, and the behavior of qc maps … the tautness comparison'). No blueprint packet exists for C4 yet, so there is no node id. Explicitly 'prove the valuative criteria'. The adic-space analogue is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-proper-partially-proper (Huber 1.3.9), for analytic adic spaces only.

items.name: Proposition 18.3 (moreover): extension over (R,R⁺) for proper maps
items.statement: If f : Y′ → Y is proper, then for every perfectoid Tate ring R with an open and integrally closed subring R⁺ ⊂ R and every commutative square Spa(R,R°) → Y′, Spa(R,R⁺) → Y, there exists a unique map Spa(R,R⁺) → Y′ making the diagram commute.
items.note: Proved in the converse direction of the proof of 18.3, using Propositions 10.10 and 12.15, Corollary 10.6 and Lemma 2.5. C4 'valuative criteria'.

items.name: Definition 18.4: partially proper map and partially proper v-stack
items.statement: A map f : Y′ → Y of v-stacks is partially proper if f is separated and, for every perfectoid Tate ring R with an open and integrally closed subring R⁺ ⊂ R and every commutative square Spa(R,R°) → Y′, Spa(R,R⁺) → Y, there exists a (necessarily unique) map Spa(R,R⁺) → Y′ making the diagram commute. A v-stack Y is partially proper if Y → ∗ is partially proper. (By Proposition 10.9 one may replace 'separated' by '0-truncated and quasiseparated'.)
items.note: C4 ('Build ECD §18 … define properness, prove the valuative criteria, and construct the partially proper envelope/canonical compactification with its universal property … functoriality, base-change compatibility, the affinoid formula over a strictly totally disconnected base, and the behavior of qc maps … the tautness comparison'). No blueprint packet exists for C4 yet, so there is no node id. Remark 18.5 explains why 'Y proper' is deliberately left undefined. Huber's adic notion is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/partially-proper-morphism, which is not this v-stack definition.

items.name: Proposition 18.6 (construction): canonical compactification Ȳ′^{/Y}
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of v-stacks. The functor sending a totally disconnected perfectoid space X = Spa(R,R⁺) over Y to Y′(R,R°) ×_{Y(R,R°)} Y(R,R⁺) extends to a v-stack Ȳ′^{/Y} with a map f̄^{/Y} : Ȳ′^{/Y} → Y and a natural map Y′ → Ȳ′^{/Y} over Y. This is the canonical compactification of f, and its formation is functorial in f.
items.note: C4 ('Build ECD §18 … define properness, prove the valuative criteria, and construct the partially proper envelope/canonical compactification with its universal property … functoriality, base-change compatibility, the affinoid formula over a strictly totally disconnected base, and the behavior of qc maps … the tautness comparison'). No blueprint packet exists for C4 yet, so there is no node id. The classical analogue is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/universal-compactification (Huber, Hub96 5.1.5), for adic spaces only.

items.name: Proposition 18.6: partial properness and universal property of the canonical compactification
items.statement: In the situation above, f̄^{/Y} : Ȳ′^{/Y} → Y is partially proper, and for every partially proper map g : Z → Y of v-stacks, composition with Y′ → Ȳ′^{/Y} induces a bijection Hom_Y(Ȳ′^{/Y}, Z) → Hom_Y(Y′, Z).
items.note: C4 plans this explicitly ('canonical compactification with its universal property'). The proof uses Lemma 7.6, Proposition 10.10 and Proposition 18.7(i).

items.name: Construction after Proposition 18.6: Ȳ for a separated v-sheaf
items.statement: For a separated v-sheaf Y, Ȳ is the v-sheaf with Ȳ(R,R⁺) = Y(R,R°) for totally disconnected Spa(R,R⁺). It comes with an injective map Y → Ȳ, and for a map Y′ → Y of separated v-sheaves, Ȳ′^{/Y} = Ȳ′ ×_{Ȳ} Y.
items.note: C4 plans this under the 'partially proper envelope' construction. No node exists.

items.name: Proposition 18.7(i)
items.statement: Let Y be a separated v-sheaf. Ȳ is partially proper.
items.note: Uses (iv)–(vi) and Z = Spa(F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))). C4 'partially proper envelope'. No node exists.

items.name: Proposition 18.7(ii)
items.statement: Let Y be a separated v-sheaf. If Y is a small v-sheaf, then Ȳ is a small v-sheaf.
items.note: C4: 'Maintain its actual small v-stack/diamond type'. No node exists.

items.name: Proposition 18.7(iii)
items.statement: Let Y be a separated v-sheaf. If Y is a diamond, then Ȳ is a diamond.
items.note: C4: 'Maintain its actual small v-stack/diamond type'. C4 also warns not to assert spatiality. No node exists.

items.name: Proposition 18.7(iv)
items.statement: Let Y be a separated v-sheaf. If Y = Spa(R,R⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid space, then Ȳ = Spa(R,(R⁺)′), where (R⁺)′ ⊂ R⁺ is the smallest open and integrally closed subring, namely the integral closure of F_p + R°°.
items.note: C4 explicitly: 'the affinoid formula over a strictly totally disconnected base'. No node exists.

items.name: Proposition 18.7(v)
items.statement: Let Y be a separated v-sheaf. The functor Y ↦ Ȳ commutes with all limits.
items.note: C4 'base-change compatibility'. No node exists.

items.name: Proposition 18.7(vi)
items.statement: Let Y be a separated v-sheaf. If f : Y′ → Y is a surjective map of separated v-sheaves, then f̄ : Ȳ′ → Ȳ is a surjective map of v-sheaves.
items.note: C4 plans all of §18. This part is not named separately. No node exists.

items.name: Proposition 18.7(vii)
items.statement: Let Y be a separated v-sheaf. If f : Y′ → Y is a quasicompact map of separated v-sheaves, then f̄ : Ȳ′ → Ȳ is proper.
items.note: C4 explicitly: 'the behavior of qc maps'. No node exists.

items.name: Proposition 18.7(viii)
items.statement: Let Y be a separated v-sheaf. If f : Y′ → Y is a quasi-pro-étale map of separated v-sheaves, then f̄ : Ȳ′ → Ȳ is quasi-pro-étale.
items.note: Uses Corollary 7.22. C4 plans all of §18. This part is not named separately. No node exists.

items.name: Corollary 18.8 (i)–(vii): relative canonical compactification
items.statement: Let Y′ → Y be a separated map of v-stacks. (i) Ȳ′^{/Y} → Y is partially proper. (ii) If Y and Y′ are small v-stacks, then Ȳ′^{/Y} is a small v-stack. (iii) If Y and Y′ are diamonds, then Ȳ′^{/Y} is a diamond. (iv) The functor Y′ ↦ Ȳ′^{/Y} from v-sheaves over Y to v-sheaves over Y commutes with all limits. (v) If f : Y′₂ → Y′₁ is a surjective map of separated v-stacks over Y, then f̄^{/Y} : Ȳ′₂^{/Y} → Ȳ′₁^{/Y} is a surjective map of v-stacks. (vi) If f : Y′₂ → Y′₁ is a quasicompact map of separated v-stacks over Y, then f̄^{/Y} is proper. (vii) If f : Y′₂ → Y′₁ is a quasi-pro-étale map of separated v-stacks over Y, then f̄^{/Y} is quasi-pro-étale.
items.note: All parts are proved together, by base change to affinoid perfectoid Y and the formula Ȳ′^{/Y} = Ȳ′ ×_{Ȳ} Y. C4: 'functoriality, base-change compatibility … behavior of qc maps'.

items.name: Claim in proof of Proposition 18.9: images of proper maps into separated maps
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of v-sheaves. If Z → Y is a proper map of v-sheaves and Z → Y′ is a map over Y, then the (sheaf-theoretic) image Z′ of Z in Y′ is proper over Y and closed in Y′.
items.note: This is an intermediate claim; C4 plans all of §18. No node exists.

items.name: Proposition 18.9: partially proper = filtered colimit of proper along closed immersions
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of v-sheaves. Then f is partially proper if and only if f can be written as a (possibly large) filtered colimit of proper maps f_i : Y′_i → Y along closed immersions Y′_i → Y′_j. If Y′ is small, then the filtered colimit can be taken small.
items.note: C4 plans all of §18 but does not name 18.9. The proof uses 18.3, 18.6 and 18.8(vi).

items.name: Taut locally spectral space ([Hub96, Definition 5.1.2])
items.statement: A locally spectral topological space T is taut if it is quasiseparated and, for every quasicompact open U ⊂ T, the closure Ū ⊂ T is quasicompact.
items.locator: recalled before the proof of Proposition 18.10, p. 107, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/taut-spaces-and-morphisms (parent stage H3) states exactly this definition. Mathlib and Tau Ceti have spectral-space API (SpectralSpace, TauCeti.IsProConstructible) but no tautness.

items.name: Proposition 18.10: partial properness via tautness for locally spatial sources
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map from a locally spatial v-sheaf Y′ to a spatial v-sheaf Y. Then f is partially proper if and only if |Y′| is taut and, for every perfectoid field K with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K and every commutative square Spa(K,O_K) → Y′, Spa(K,K⁺) → Y, there exists a unique map Spa(K,K⁺) → Y′ making the diagram commute.
items.note: C4 explicitly: 'Prove the tautness comparison in its stated locally spatial scope'. No node exists. The proof has two misprints (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Definition/Proposition 19.1: extension by zero f_! for étale maps
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be an étale morphism of small v-stacks. Then f* : D_ét(Y,Λ) → D_ét(Y′,Λ) has a left adjoint Rf_! : D_ét(Y′,Λ) → D_ét(Y,Λ). Rf_! commutes with canonical truncations and is also written f_!.
items.note: C5 explicitly: 'Construct the exact left adjoint to pullback for étale maps (19.1), first on perfectoid/étale sites and then by enhanced hyperdescent'. No packet node exists. It is built via the simplicial description D_ét(Y,Λ) ≅ D_cart(Y_•,ét,Λ) of Proposition 17.3 (C2/E2).

items.name: Definition/Proposition 19.1: base change for f_!
items.statement: In the situation of 19.1, for every map g : Ỹ → Y of small v-stacks with pullbacks f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ and g′ : Ỹ′ → Y′, the natural transformation Rf̃_! g′* → g* Rf_! of functors D_ét(Y′,Λ) → D_ét(Ỹ,Λ), adjoint to g′* → g′* f* Rf_! = f̃* g* Rf_!, is an equivalence.
items.note: C5: 'Prove its base-change law and its agreement with extension by zero for an open immersion'.

items.name: Theorem 19.2 (construction): the exchange map j_! Rg_* → Rf_* j′_!
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a proper morphism of small v-stacks and j : U ⊂ Y an open immersion, with pullbacks g : U′ = U ×_Y Y′ → U and j′ : U′ ⊂ Y′. There is a natural transformation j_! Rg_* → Rf_* j′_! : D_ét(U′,Λ) → D_ét(Y,Λ), adjoint to f* j_! Rg_* = j′_! g* Rg_* → j′_! (base change for j_! from 19.1, then the counit).
items.locator: Theorem 19.2, p. 108 (map constructed on p. 109), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: C5 explicitly constructs j_!Rg_*A → Rf_*j′_!A. The printed statement has 'U′ = V ×_Y Y′' (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Theorem 19.2: proper base change (bounded below)
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 19.2, if f is quasi-pro-étale or nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p, then for every A ∈ D⁺_ét(U′,Λ) the map j_! Rg_* A → Rf_* j′_! A is an isomorphism.
items.note: C5 plans this explicitly, keeping both hypotheses. The classical adic analogue is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/proper-base-change-extension-by-zero (locally noetherian adic spaces, not diamonds). The proof reduces via Propositions 17.6 and 19.1 to X = Spa(C,C⁺). Note that Proposition 17.6 is stated only for nΛ = 0, so the quasi-pro-étale case really rests on Corollary 16.8(i). It then uses a hypercover by canonical compactifications of strictly totally disconnected spaces ([BS15, 3.3.6]), a Leray reduction to connected Y′ = Spa(C′, C′°°+C⁺) and Lemma 19.4.

items.name: Theorem 19.2: proper base change (unbounded, finite cohomological dimension)
items.statement: If moreover Rf_* has finite cohomological dimension, i.e. there is an integer N such that R^i f_* A = 0 for i > N for all A ∈ D_ét(Y′,Λ) concentrated in degree 0, then j_! Rg_* A → Rf_* j′_! A is an isomorphism for all A ∈ D_ét(U′,Λ). (The proof reduces to the D⁺ case, so it tacitly keeps the hypothesis that f is quasi-pro-étale or nΛ = 0 with n prime to p.)
items.note: C5: 'retain these hypotheses when using a cohomological-dimension bound to pass to the unbounded case'.

items.name: Lemma 19.4: acyclicity of relative Zariski–Riemann spaces off the special fibre
items.statement: Let K ⊂ K′ be algebraically closed fields and V ⊂ K a valuation ring of K. Let T′ = Spa(K′,V) be the spectral space of valuation rings V′ ⊂ K′ containing V, T = Spa(K,V), f : T′ → T the map V′ ↦ V′ ∩ K, and s ∈ T the closed point (corresponding to V). If F is a sheaf of torsion abelian groups on T′ with F_{x′} = 0 for all x′ ∈ f⁻¹(s), then RΓ(T′,F) = 0.
items.note: C5 plans this explicitly: 'Zariski–Riemann spaces, and proper base change for schemes. Construct the Zariski–Riemann models and their limit/cohomology comparisons, including the henselian-ring result cited as Huber [Hub93b]'. Related nodes are ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/zariski-riemann-space-as-limit and …/etale-over-normal-separably-closed-local-isomorphism (Hub93b 2.1 and 2.4). …/zariski-riemann-cohomology-vanishing is a neighbouring but different statement (constant coefficients). No node for 19.4 itself.

items.name: Theorem 19.5(i): invariance under change of algebraically closed base field
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Assume Y lives over k, a discrete algebraically closed field of characteristic p, and let k′/k be an extension of discrete algebraically closed fields and Y′ = Y ×_k k′. Then pullback D_ét(Y,Λ) → D_ét(Y′,Λ) is fully faithful.
items.note: C6: 'Prove all three cases of Theorem 19.5 … The conclusion is full faithfulness of pullback on D_ét'. Deduced from (ii) and (iii). No packet node exists.

items.name: Theorem 19.5(ii): invariance under change of algebraically closed base field
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Assume Y lives over k, an algebraically closed discrete field of characteristic p. Let C/k be an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field and Y′ = Y ×_k Spa(C,C⁺) for some open and bounded valuation subring C⁺ ⊂ C containing k. Then pullback D_ét(Y,Λ) → D_ét(Y′,Λ) is fully faithful.
items.note: C6: 'Prove all three cases of Theorem 19.5 … The conclusion is full faithfulness of pullback on D_ét'. Reduced to C the completed algebraic closure of k((t)). Then the argument uses annuli Y′_n = {|t|ⁿ ≤ |ϖ| ≤ |t|^{1/n}}, Theorem 19.2, Proposition 14.9 and annulus cohomology (H4). The step invoking Theorem 19.2 for the non-proper f_n is recorded as a gap in sourceIssues. No packet node exists.

items.name: Theorem 19.5(iii): invariance under change of algebraically closed base field
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Assume Y lives over Spa(C,C⁺), with C algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean and C⁺ ⊂ C open and bounded valuation subring. Let C′/C be an extension of algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean fields and C′⁺ ⊂ C′ an open and bounded valuation subring containing C⁺ such that Spa(C′,C′⁺) → Spa(C,C⁺) is surjective. Then for Y′ = Y ×_{Spa(C,C⁺)} Spa(C′,C′⁺), pullback D_ét(Y,Λ) → D_ét(Y′,Λ) is fully faithful.
items.note: C6: 'Prove all three cases of Theorem 19.5 … The conclusion is full faithfulness of pullback on D_ét'. Proved via Postnikov completeness, Proposition 17.6 and the final paragraph of Theorem 16.1. No packet node exists.

items.name: Black box: ℓ-adic cohomology of annuli over Spa(C′,C′⁺)
items.statement: For C′ an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field with open bounded valuation subring C′⁺, ℓ ≠ p, and a (perfectoid) annulus A = {|ϖ|ⁿ ≤ |t| ≤ |ϖ|^{1/n}} over Spa(C′,C′⁺), one has H^i(A,F_ℓ) = F_ℓ for i = 0, 1 and H^i(A,F_ℓ) = 0 otherwise; the H¹-class is the Kummer class of the coordinate, which dies after extracting ℓ-power roots of it.
items.locator: used in the proof of Theorem 19.5(ii), p. 112, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Stage H4: 'Prove the prime-to-p cohomology and restriction maps for the discs, punctured discs and annuli used in ECD 19.5 and 24.1. Include Kummer classes …'. No node exists (the H0 packet covers only H0–H3).

items.name: Black box: proper base change theorem in étale cohomology of schemes
items.statement: For a proper morphism of schemes X → S and a torsion abelian étale sheaf F on X, the formation of R f_* F commutes with base change. In particular, for S = Spec V with V a valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field (a strictly henselian local ring), RΓ(X,F) ≅ RΓ(X_s, F|_{X_s}) for the closed fibre X_s.
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemma 19.4, p. 110, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: No atlas stage owns scheme-theoretic proper base change. C5 and AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5 only use it. Mathlib has the small étale site (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.smallEtaleTopology) but no étale cohomology base-change theorems. The nearest planned statement is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/affine-henselian-comparison-3-2-5 (Gabber's affine analogue for henselian pairs), which is not the proper-morphism theorem.

items.name: Black box [Hub93b, Lemma 2.1]: Zariski–Riemann space as a limit of models
items.statement: With C the cofiltered category of proper V-schemes X with a point x ∈ X(K′), T′ = Spa(K′,V) ≅ lim_C |X|. One may restrict to integral projective X with x dominant.
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemma 19.4, p. 110, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/zariski-riemann-space-as-limit (projective integral models over a ring).

items.name: Black box [Hub93b, Lemma 2.4]: étale and Zariski topoi agree in the limit
items.statement: The topoi lim_C |X|^∼ and lim_C X_ét^∼ are equivalent, since any étale map becomes a local isomorphism after some pullback in C.
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemma 19.4, p. 110, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/etale-over-normal-separably-closed-local-isomorphism (Huber 1993 Lemma 2.4: étale maps to closed subschemes of a normal integral scheme with separably closed function field are local isomorphisms). The passage to the limit topos is part of C5.

items.name: Definition 20.1(i): constructible sheaf on a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space
items.statement: Let Λ be a noetherian ring and X a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space; identify étale sheaves on X with sheaves on |X|. A sheaf F of Λ-modules on X_ét is constructible if there is a (finite) stratification of |X| into constructible locally closed subsets S_i such that each F|_{S_i} is the constant sheaf on S_i associated with a finitely generated Λ-module.
items.note: C7: 'Implement all of §20's sheaf-level constructibility and descent results with spectral constructible stratifications'. No packet node exists. Mathlib has Topology.IsConstructible (constructible subsets) only. The classical adic analogue is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/classical-constructible-sheaves, which uses a different setting.

items.name: Definition 20.1(ii): constructible sheaf on a small v-stack
items.statement: Let Λ be noetherian, Y a small v-stack and F a small sheaf of Λ-modules on Y_v. F is constructible if F ∈ D_ét(Y,Λ) ⊂ D(Y,Λ) and, for every strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space f : X → Y, the pullback f*F is constructible in the sense of (i).

items.name: Constructible sheaf on a spectral space (implicit in Lemma 20.4)
items.statement: For a spectral space X and noetherian Λ, a sheaf of Λ-modules on X is constructible if there is a finite stratification of X into constructible locally closed subsets on each of which it is constant with finitely generated value (the analogue of 20.1(i) for |X|).
items.note: C7 'spectral constructible stratifications'. Mathlib has constructible subsets (Topology.IsConstructible) but no constructible sheaves.

items.name: Remark 20.3: constructible sheaves form an abelian category
items.statement: The class of constructible sheaves (Definition 20.1) is stable under kernels, cokernels, images and extensions; in particular constructible sheaves form an abelian category.
items.note: C7: 'stability under the appropriate operations'. The source only sketches the argument (reduction to maps of constant sheaves on refined strata).

items.name: Lemma 20.4(a): constructible = compact on a spectral space
items.statement: Let Λ be noetherian, X a spectral space and F a sheaf of Λ-modules on X. Then F is constructible if and only if F is compact in the category of sheaves of Λ-modules on X, i.e. Hom(F,−) commutes with filtered colimits.
items.note: C7 plans all sheaf-level constructibility results of §20. No node exists.

items.name: Lemma 20.4(b): sheaves on a spectral space are filtered colimits of constructible sheaves
items.statement: Let Λ be noetherian and X a spectral space. Every sheaf of Λ-modules on X is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves.
items.note: C7. The classical analogue ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-sheaf-colimit-of-constructible is for locally noetherian adic spaces, not arbitrary spectral spaces.

items.name: Proposition 20.5: v-descent of constructibility
items.statement: Let Λ be noetherian, f : Ỹ → Y a surjective map of small v-stacks and F a small sheaf of Λ-modules on Y_v. If f*F is constructible, then F is constructible.
items.note: C7 'descent'. No node exists.

items.name: Proposition 20.6: characterizations of constructible sheaves on spatial diamonds
items.statement: Let Λ be noetherian, Y a spatial diamond and F an étale sheaf of Λ-modules on Y. The following are equivalent: (i) F is constructible; (ii) F is compact in the category of étale sheaves of Λ-modules on Y; (iii) there is a stratification of |Y| into constructible locally closed subsets S_i such that, for every strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space f : X → Y, f*F|_{f⁻¹(S_i)} is the constant sheaf associated with a finitely generated Λ-module.
items.note: C7. The proof uses Lemma 11.31 and 'strongly constructible' sheaves (condition (iii)).
