items.name: Proposition 20.6 (moreover): étale sheaves are filtered colimits of constructible sheaves
items.statement: Let Λ be noetherian and Y a spatial diamond. Every étale sheaf of Λ-modules on Y is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves.

items.name: Proposition 20.7: constructible sheaves in cofiltered limits
items.statement: Let Y_i (i ∈ I) be a cofiltered inverse system of spatial diamonds with inverse limit Y = lim_i Y_i a spatial diamond, and Λ noetherian. With Cons(−,Λ) the category of constructible étale sheaves of Λ-modules, the natural functor 2-colim_i Cons(Y_i,Λ) → Cons(Y,Λ) is an equivalence.
items.note: C7 'finite-stage descent'. Uses Proposition 14.9 (relative version) and Proposition 11.23.

items.name: L|_Z (before Proposition 20.8)
items.statement: For an étale U → Y, a constructible closed Z ⊂ U with open complement j′ : U ∖ Z → U, and a sheaf L on U, L|_Z is the cokernel of the injective map j′_!(L|_{U∖Z}) → L. The derived analogue is used in 20.16–20.17.
items.note: C7: 'the filtration by extensions of local systems supported on locally closed constructible subsets'.

items.name: Proposition 20.8: dévissage of constructible sheaves on spatial diamonds
items.statement: Let Λ be noetherian and Y a spatial diamond. An étale sheaf F of Λ-modules on Y is constructible if and only if F has a (finite) filtration whose graded pieces are of the form j_!(L|_Z), where j : U → Y is a quasicompact separated étale map, Z ⊂ U a constructible closed subset, and L a sheaf of Λ-modules on U locally on U_ét isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finitely generated Λ-module.
items.note: C7 plans this explicitly. The proof localizes at points via 20.7 and uses the profinite groups G_S ⊂ G_η of a local spatial diamond.

items.name: Proposition 20.9: compactness of constructible F_ℓ-sheaves against bounded-below colimits
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond and F a constructible étale sheaf of F_ℓ-vector spaces on Y. For every filtered direct system C_j ∈ D^{≥−n}_ét(Y,F_ℓ), j ∈ J (uniformly bounded to the left), the natural map colim_j Hom_{D_ét(Y,F_ℓ)}(F[0],C_j) → Hom_{D_ét(Y,F_ℓ)}(F[0], colim_j C_j) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C9/bounded-filtered-compactness (C8 packet, part C9).

items.name: Proposition 20.10(a): left-completeness under finite ℓ-cohomological dimension
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond and assume there is an integer N with H^i(Y_ét,F) = 0 for i > N for all ℓ-torsion sheaves F on Y_ét. Then D(Y_ét,F_ℓ) is left-complete, and hence D(Y_ét,F_ℓ) = D_ét(Y,F_ℓ).
items.note: Nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C9/uniform-test-bound (the bound passes to qc separated étale U, via Remark 21.14), C9/left-completeness and C9/ordinary-derived-comparison.

items.name: Proposition 20.10(b): compact objects with F_ℓ-coefficients
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of 20.10(a), D(Y_ét,F_ℓ) is compactly generated (by the j_!F_ℓ for quasicompact separated étale j : U → Y), and a complex C ∈ D_ét(Y,F_ℓ) is compact if and only if it is bounded and all its cohomology sheaves are constructible.
items.note: Nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C9/finite-field-compact-objects, C9/compact-generators, C9/global-sections-coproducts and C9/etale-constant-compact.

items.name: Definition 20.11(i): perfect-constructible complex on a strictly totally disconnected space
items.statement: Let Λ be any ring and X a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space. A ∈ D_ét(X,Λ) ≅ D(|X|,Λ) is perfect-constructible if there is a stratification of X into constructible locally closed subsets S_i ⊂ |X| such that A|_{S_i} is the constant sheaf on S_i associated with a perfect complex of Λ-modules.
items.note: C7: 'For arbitrary commutative Λ, define perfect-constructible complexes by the appropriate finite stratifications and constant perfect complexes'.

items.name: Definition 20.11(ii): perfect-constructible complex on a small v-stack
items.statement: Let Y be a small v-stack and A ∈ D_ét(Y,Λ). A is perfect-constructible if, for every strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space f : X → Y, f*A ∈ D_ét(X,Λ) is perfect-constructible.

items.name: Perfect-constructible complexes form a thick subcategory D_ét,pc(Y,Λ)
items.statement: The perfect-constructible complexes form a thick triangulated subcategory D_ét,pc(Y,Λ) ⊂ D_ét(Y,Λ).
items.note: The source says 'It is clear'. C7 plans all of §20 but does not name this claim.

items.name: Proposition 20.12: perfect-constructible via cohomology sheaves and stalks
items.statement: Let Λ be noetherian, Y a small v-stack and A ∈ D_ét(Y,Λ). A is perfect-constructible if and only if A is locally bounded, each cohomology sheaf H^i(A) is a constructible sheaf of Λ-modules, and all geometric stalks of A are perfect complexes of Λ-modules.
items.note: C7: 'Prove the equivalent stalk/perfectness and locally bounded Tor-amplitude conditions with their hypotheses'.

items.name: Proposition 20.13: v-descent of perfect-constructibility
items.statement: Let Λ be a ring, f : Ỹ → Y a surjective map of small v-stacks and A ∈ D_ét(Y,Λ). If f*A ∈ D_ét(Ỹ,Λ) is perfect-constructible, then A is perfect-constructible.
items.note: C7 explicitly: 'and v-descent'.

items.name: Proposition 20.14: restricted compactness of perfect-constructible complexes
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond and A ∈ D_ét(Y,Λ) perfect-constructible. Then for every filtered direct system C_j ∈ D^{≥−n}_ét(Y,Λ), j ∈ J (uniformly bounded to the left), the natural map colim_j Hom_{D_ét(Y,Λ)}(A,C_j) → Hom_{D_ét(Y,Λ)}(A, colim_j C_j) is an isomorphism. (The paper prints F_ℓ instead of Λ for the C_j and the Hom-categories; see sourceIssues.)
items.note: Not named by any stage description or node. C7 plans 20.15, whose full-faithfulness step (and 20.16's final step) uses 20.14, so it is an unstated prerequisite. C9 covers only the F_ℓ, constructible-sheaf case 20.9 (node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C9/bounded-filtered-compactness), not perfect-constructible complexes over a general Λ.

items.name: Proposition 20.15(a): perfect-constructible complexes in cofiltered limits of spaces
items.statement: Let Y_i (i ∈ I) be a cofiltered inverse system of spatial diamonds with inverse limit Y = lim_i Y_i a spatial diamond, and Λ a ring. The natural functor 2-colim_i D_ét,pc(Y_i,Λ) → D_ét,pc(Y,Λ) is an equivalence.
items.note: C7 explicitly flags the proof order: prove full faithfulness first (it uses 20.14), then 20.16, then essential surjectivity.

items.name: Proposition 20.15(b): perfect-constructible complexes under filtered colimits of rings
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond and Λ = colim_i Λ_i a filtered colimit of rings. The natural functor 2-colim_i D_ét,pc(Y,Λ_i) → D_ét,pc(Y,Λ) is an equivalence.
items.note: C7 names 20.15 as a whole. The ring-colimit part is 'proved similarly' in the source (no separate proof).

items.name: Proposition 20.16: characterizations of perfect-constructible complexes on spatial diamonds
items.statement: Let Λ be a ring, Y a spatial diamond and A ∈ D_ét(Y,Λ). The following are equivalent: (i) A is perfect-constructible; (ii) there is a stratification of |Y| into constructible locally closed subsets S_i such that, for every strictly totally disconnected perfectoid f : X → Y, f*A|_{f⁻¹(S_i)} is the constant sheaf associated with a perfect complex of Λ-modules; (iii) A has a finite filtration whose graded pieces are j_!(L|_Z), with j : U → Y quasicompact separated étale, Z ⊂ U constructible closed, and L ∈ D_ét(U,Λ) locally constant with perfect values.
items.note: C7 plans this explicitly. The (i)⇒(ii) step has a justification gap (see sourceIssues).

items.name: Proposition 20.17(a): left-completeness under bounded Λ-cohomological dimension
items.statement: Let Λ be a ring and Y a spatial diamond of bounded Λ-cohomological dimension. Then D(Y_ét,Λ) is left-complete, so D_ét(Y,Λ) = D(Y_ét,Λ).
items.note: Nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C9/uniform-test-bound, C9/left-completeness and C9/ordinary-derived-comparison.

items.name: Proposition 20.17(b): compact objects are the perfect-constructible complexes
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of 20.17(a), A ∈ D_ét(Y,Λ) is compact if and only if A is perfect-constructible, and D_ét(Y,Λ) is compactly generated, with compact generators j_!Λ for j : U → Y ranging over quasicompact separated étale maps.
items.note: Nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C9/compact-iff-perfect-constructible, C9/compact-generators, C9/compact-implies-perfect-constructible, C9/perfect-constructible-implies-compact and C9/perfect-local-system-compact. The printed 'j : U → X' is already recorded as DiamondEtaleCohomology/E2.

items.name: Black box [Sta, Tag 0719]: finite cohomological dimension implies left-completeness
items.statement: On a ringed site, if there is a basis of objects U and an integer d with H^p(U,F) = 0 for all p > d and all sheaves of modules F, then every E ∈ D(O) satisfies E ≅ R lim_n τ^{≥−n}E; in particular D(O) is left-complete.
items.locator: used in the proofs of Propositions 20.10 and 20.17, pp. 117, 121, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/postnikov-finite-cohomological-dimension. The C8/C9 packet also files a request to E2 for the site-level form ('the ringed-space statement alone is insufficient').

items.name: Definition 21.1(i): dimension of a locally spectral space
items.statement: Let X be a locally spectral space. dim X ∈ Z_{≥0} ∪ {−∞,∞} is the supremum of all integers n for which there is a chain x_0,…,x_n of distinct points of X with x_i a specialization of x_{i+1} for i = 0,…,n−1.
items.note: This is Order.krullDim (Specialization X) (Mathlib: Specialization with its specialization partial order for T0 spaces; krullDim : WithBot ℕ∞ = sup of LTSeries lengths). Chains of distinct points under specialization are exactly the LTSeries, with ⊥ for empty X. The atlas plans to use mathlib:topologicalKrullDim and prove the equality for quasi-sober T0 spaces: node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/specialization-dimension (stage C8).

items.name: Definition 21.1(ii): dimension of a spectral map
items.statement: Let f : X′ → X be a spectral map of locally spectral spaces. Then dim f = sup_{x ∈ X} dim f⁻¹(x) ∈ Z_{≥0} ∪ {−∞,∞}.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/fibre-dimension.

items.name: Definition 21.2: topological transcendence degree tr.c
items.statement: Let K ⊂ K′ be an extension of complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields. tr.c(K′/K) ∈ Z_{≥0} ∪ {∞} is the minimum of all integers n such that there is a dense subfield L ⊂ K′ containing K with transcendence degree n over K.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/topological-trdeg.

items.name: Comparison of Definition 21.2 with [Hub96, Definition 1.8.2]
items.statement: For extensions of algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean fields, tr.c(K′/K) as in Definition 21.2 agrees with Huber's topological transcendence degree [Hub96, Definition 1.8.2] (checked using Krasner's lemma).
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/finite-topological-generators. The C8 packet gap 'Krasner comparison and finite topological generators' notes the source gives only an assertion ('as one easily checks').

items.name: Black box: Krasner's lemma
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean valued field and L/K algebraic, with the norm of L extending that of K. If x ∈ L is separable over K with all conjugates in L, y ∈ L is integral over K, and |x − y| < |x − x′| for every conjugate x′ ≠ x of x, then x ∈ K(y).
items.locator: used in the remark after Definition 21.2, p. 122, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Krasner.lean: instance IsKrasner.of_completeSpace [NontriviallyNormedField K] [CompleteSpace K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [NormedAlgebra K L] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K L], with the conclusion packaged as IsKrasner.krasner.

items.name: Lemma 21.3(i): subadditivity of tr.c in towers
items.statement: Let K ⊂ K′ ⊂ K″ be extensions of algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean fields. Then tr.c(K″/K) ≤ tr.c(K″/K′) + tr.c(K′/K).
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/topological-trdeg-tower. = [Hub96, Remark 1.8.3(i)].

items.name: Lemma 21.3(ii): tr.c under dense compositum
items.statement: Let K ⊂ K′ and L ⊂ L′ be extensions of algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean fields with an embedding K′ ↪ L′ sending K into L such that the algebraic closure of L·K′ in L′ is dense. Then tr.c(L′/L) ≤ tr.c(K′/K).
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/topological-trdeg-base-change. = [Hub96, Remark 1.8.3(ii)]; the source says 'Similarly, one proves'.

items.name: Black box (Temkin): monotonicity of tr.c when finite
items.statement: Let K ⊂ K′ ⊂ K″ be extensions of algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean fields. If tr.c(K′/K) < ∞, then tr.c(K′/K) ≤ tr.c(K″/K). ([Tem21, Theorem 3.2.3] identifies a finite tr.c with the maximal number of topologically algebraically independent elements, which is monotone by [Tem21, Lemma 2.2.2].) The general case is Question 21.4, left open.
items.note: Only as C8 packet gap 'Temkin finite-degree paragraph and remaining dimension API' (source not yet read in full). No node exists. Stage C8 forbids assuming the general monotonicity of Question 21.4.

items.name: Definition (after Question 21.4): modified topological transcendence degree tr.c̃
items.statement: For an extension K ⊂ K′ of complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields, tr.c̃(K′/K) is the minimum of tr.c(K″/K) over all complete algebraically closed extensions K″ of K′.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/modified-topological-trdeg, with a universe-bound caveat. Stage C8: 'Preserve the minimum over further complete algebraically closed extensions in tr.c-tilde'.

items.name: Properties of tr.c̃: tr.c̃ ≤ tr.c and Lemma 21.3 holds for tr.c̃
items.statement: tr.c̃(K′/K) ≤ tr.c(K′/K), and both parts of Lemma 21.3 hold with tr.c̃ in place of tr.c.
items.note: Nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/modified-trdeg-tower and C8/modified-trdeg-base-change (gap: valued amalgamation). The trivial inequality tr.c̃ ≤ tr.c has no own node.

items.name: Definition 21.5: dim.tr̃ of a map of analytic adic spaces
items.statement: Let f : X′ → X be a map of analytic adic spaces. dim.tr̃ f ∈ Z_{≥0} ∪ {−∞,∞} is the supremum over x′ ∈ X′ of tr.c̃(C(x′)/C(x)), where x = f(x′) and C(x′), C(x) are completed algebraic closures of the completed residue fields.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/analytic-dim-trg.

items.name: Lemma 21.6: dim f ≤ dim.tr̃ f
items.statement: Let f : X′ → X be a map of analytic adic spaces. Then dim f ≤ dim.tr̃ f.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/analytic-dimension-bound. The proof reruns [Hub96, Lemma 1.8.5(i)]; C8 packet gap 'Huber valuative dimension and completion lemmas'.

items.name: Black box [Hub96, Lemma 1.8.5(i)]: dimension bounded by transcendence dimension
items.statement: For a morphism f of analytic adic spaces, dim f ≤ dim.tr f (Huber's version with tr.c), proved by bounding chain lengths through rational value-group ranks and residue transcendence degrees.
items.locator: used in the proof of Lemma 21.6, p. 123, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Covered only through node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/analytic-dimension-bound and the packet gap 'Huber valuative dimension and completion lemmas'. Huber's lemma itself has no node.

items.name: Definition 21.7(a): dim.tr̃ of a map of diamonds
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a map of diamonds. For each y′ ∈ |Y′| with image y ∈ |Y|, choose quasi-pro-étale maps Spa(C(y),C(y)⁺) → Y with y in the image and Spa(C(y′),C(y′)⁺) → Spa(C(y),C(y)⁺) ×_Y Y′ with y′ in the image. Then dim.tr̃ f ∈ Z_{≥0} ∪ {−∞,∞} is the supremum of tr.c̃(C(y′)/C(y)) over y′ ∈ |Y′|.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/diamond-dim-trg (requires proving independence of choices, which the source leaves implicit).

items.name: Definition 21.7(b): dim.tr̃ of a map of v-stacks representable in diamonds
items.statement: If f : Y′ → Y is a map of v-stacks that is representable in diamonds, dim.tr̃ f is the supremum of dim.tr̃(f ×_Y X) over all maps X → Y from diamonds X.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/diamond-dim-trg (second sentence).

items.name: Remark 21.8: dim.tr̃ does not increase under pullback
items.statement: Pullback does not increase dim.tr̃ (by Lemma 21.3(ii) for tr.c̃); hence the definition of dim.tr̃ f for maps of v-stacks representable in diamonds agrees with Definition 21.7(a) when Y and Y′ are diamonds.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/diamond-dim-base-change.

items.name: Remark 21.8: dim Y and dim f for locally spatial diamonds
items.statement: If Y is a locally spatial diamond, dim Y := dim |Y| (Definition 21.1). If f : Y′ → Y is a map of v-stacks representable in locally spatial diamonds, dim f is the supremum over locally spatial diamonds X → Y of dim(f ×_Y X). It suffices to take X of the form Spa(C,C⁺).
items.note: Stage C8 plans 'topological dimension'. Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/fibre-dimension covers spectral maps. The relative v-stack version and the reduction to X = Spa(C,C⁺) have no node.

items.name: Proposition 21.9: one-point quasiseparated diamonds (existence)
items.statement: Let Y be a quasiseparated diamond with |Y| a single point. Then Y = Spa(C,O_C)/G for an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C and a profinite group G acting continuously and faithfully on C.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/point-quotient. The proof uses Lemma 7.19.

items.name: Proposition 21.9: uniqueness of the pair (C,G)
items.statement: In Proposition 21.9, the pair (C,G) is unique up to (non-unique) isomorphism. G is the automorphism group of Spa(C,O_C) → Y.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/point-quotient-unique.

items.name: Consequence of Proposition 21.9: sheaves on a point are Galois modules
items.statement: For Y = Spa(C,O_C)/G as in Proposition 21.9, étale sheaves on Y are equivalent to discrete G-modules with continuous action, and étale cohomology of Y is continuous group cohomology of G.
items.note: Nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/point-sheaf-equivalence and C8/point-cohomology. Requests to tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology layers 0 and 10.

items.name: Definition 21.10: ℓ-cohomological dimension at a maximal point
items.statement: Let Y be a quasiseparated diamond and ℓ a prime. For a maximal point y ∈ |Y|, let Y_y ⊂ Y be the subdiamond with |Y_y| = {y} and write Y_y = Spa(C_y,O_{C_y})/G_y. Then cd_ℓ y := cd_ℓ G_y.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/point-cd. cd_ℓ of profinite groups is planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-11-cohomological-dimension.

items.name: Proposition 21.11: cohomological dimension of spatial diamonds
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond, ℓ a prime and F an ℓ-power-torsion étale sheaf on Y with F|_U = 0 for some open U ⊂ Y. Then H^i(Y,F) = 0 for i > dim(Y ∖ U) + sup_y cd_ℓ y, where y runs through the maximal points of Y.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/spatial-cohomological-bound, with supporting nodes C8/constructible-support-reduction, C8/boundary-dimension-drop and C8/local-stalk-bound. An analogue of [Hub96, Corollary 2.8.3]. The printed overline in 'V \ U \ V' is over V∖U (checked in the PDF), so the dimension-drop argument is fine.

items.name: Lemma 21.13: degree-zero direct image along quasicompact injections
items.statement: Let j : U → Y be a quasicompact injection of locally spatial diamonds. Then for any sheaf of abelian groups F on U_ét, R^i j_{ét*} F = 0 for i > 0.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/injection-direct-image. The proof uses Corollary 16.10.

items.name: Remark 21.14: degree-zero direct image along qc separated quasi-pro-étale maps
items.statement: More generally, for a quasicompact separated quasi-pro-étale morphism j : U → Y of locally spatial diamonds and any abelian sheaf F on U_ét, R^i j_{ét*} F = 0 for i > 0.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/qpetale-direct-image, with C8/strictly-disconnected-acyclic. It is used in Propositions 20.10 and 20.17 to pass cd bounds to qc separated étale U.

items.name: Proposition 21.15: local case of the cohomological bound
items.statement: Let Y be a spatial diamond such that |Y| is local, with closed point s and complement U = Y ∖ {s}. Then for every ℓ-torsion étale sheaf F on Y_ét with F|_U = 0, H^i(Y_ét,F) = 0 for all i > cd_ℓ η, where η ∈ |Y| is the unique generic point.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/closed-point-bound, with C8/specialization-stabilizers (G_s ⊂ G_η closed) and C8/closed-point-cohomology (Cartan–Leray).

items.name: Proposition 21.16: cd_ℓ of maximal points bounded by dim.tr̃
items.statement: Let f : Y → Spa(C,C⁺) be a map of locally spatial diamonds and y ∈ |Y| a maximal point. Then for all primes ℓ ≠ p, cd_ℓ y ≤ dim.tr̃ f.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/point-cd-geometric-bound. The misprint C′×/(1+C′′×) in its proof is already recorded as DiamondEtaleCohomology/E1.

items.name: Step in proof of Proposition 21.16: the wild kernel is pro-p
items.statement: For Y_y = Spa(C′,O_{C′})/G with G acting continuously and faithfully on C′ and fixing C, the closed normal subgroup P ⊂ G acting trivially on C′^×/(1 + C′°°) is a pro-p group, so cd_ℓ G = cd_ℓ G/P for ℓ ≠ p.
items.note: Nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/wild-kernel-pro-p and C8/prime-to-p-wild-removal (via Lemma 21.17).

items.name: Step in proof of Proposition 21.16: residue Galois group and its cd
items.statement: With k ⊂ k′ the residue fields of C ⊂ C′ and I ⊂ G/P the pointwise stabilizer of k′, Ḡ = G/I acts faithfully and continuously on the discrete field k′ fixing k, k′₀ = k′^Ḡ is perfect with algebraic closure k′, Gal(k′/k′₀) = Ḡ, and cd_ℓ Ḡ ≤ tr.deg(k′₀/k) = tr.deg(k′/k).
items.note: Nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/residue-galois-identification and C8/residue-cd-bound.

items.name: Step in proof of Proposition 21.16: tame inertia embedding
items.statement: The tame inertia I/P acts through homomorphisms Γ′/Γ → μ_∞(k) (Γ ⊂ Γ′ ⊂ R_{>0} the value groups). If dim_Q Γ′/Γ < ∞ this gives a (closed) embedding I/P ↪ Hom(Γ′/Γ, μ_∞(k)) ≅ (A_f^p)^{dim_Q Γ′/Γ}, hence cd_ℓ I/P ≤ dim_Q Γ′/Γ.
items.note: Nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/tame-character-embedding and C8/tame-cd-bound.

items.name: Lemma 21.17: wild automorphisms in characteristic p
items.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic p and γ a continuous automorphism of C such that γ^{n!} converges pointwise to the identity as n → ∞. If γ acts trivially on C^×/(1 + C°°), then γ^{pⁿ} converges pointwise to the identity as n → ∞.
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/wild-automorphism. It uses profinite Sylow subgroups (request to tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups layer 2). Tau Ceti has TauCeti.IsProP and TauCeti.IsProPSylow, but not this lemma.

items.name: Black box [Sch92, Corollary 4.6]: cohomological dimension of spectral spaces
items.statement: If X is a spectral space of Krull dimension ≤ d, then H^i(X,F) = 0 for all i > d and all abelian sheaves F on X.
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 21.11, p. 125, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/spectral-cohomological-bound, with C8/specialization-chain-space and C8/chain-cohomology-comparison. The packet gap notes Scheiderer's paper was not read.

items.name: Black box (Serre): Galois cohomological dimension and transcendence degree
items.statement: If k is algebraically closed, F/k a (perfect) field extension and ℓ ≠ char k, then cd_ℓ Gal(F̄/F) ≤ tr.deg(F/k).
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 21.16, p. 126, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/residue-cd-bound. The source cites no reference (standard; Serre, Galois Cohomology II.4.2).

items.name: Black box [Bou98, VI.10.3 Corollary 1]: Abhyankar inequality
items.statement: For an extension of valued fields with residue extension k′/k and value groups Γ ⊂ Γ′, tr.deg(k′/k) + dim_Q(Γ′/Γ ⊗ Q) ≤ tr.deg of the field extension. Applied through a dense subfield, and because rationalized value groups and residue transcendence degrees are unchanged by completion and only grow under further extension, this gives tr.deg(k′/k) + dim_Q Γ′/Γ ≤ tr.c̃(C′/C).
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 21.16, p. 127, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/valuation-transcendence-bound. The packet gap 'Bourbaki valuation inequality' notes the cited proof has not been read.

items.name: Black box: cd_ℓ of closed subgroups of profinite groups
items.statement: If H is a closed subgroup of a profinite group G, then cd_ℓ H ≤ cd_ℓ G.
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 21.15, p. 126, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: This is cd_p_le_of_isClosed in the ProfiniteCohomology layer 11 plan (NSW 3.3.5). It is not in the Tau Ceti library at the pinned commit.

items.name: Black box: cd_ℓ of an extension of profinite groups
items.statement: For a closed normal subgroup N of a profinite group G, cd_ℓ G ≤ cd_ℓ N + cd_ℓ G/N.
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 21.16, p. 127, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/extension-cd-bound, which requests the all-degree Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence from ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1–R02.2.

items.name: Black box: removing a pro-p normal subgroup
items.statement: If P is a closed normal pro-p subgroup of a profinite group G and ℓ ≠ p, then cd_ℓ G = cd_ℓ G/P.
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 21.16, p. 126, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: Node DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/prime-to-p-wild-removal.

items.name: Definition 22.2: compactifiable morphism
items.statement: A morphism f : Y′ → Y of v-stacks is compactifiable if it can be written as a composite of an open immersion and a partially proper morphism.
items.note: S0: 'Define compactifiability by an open immersion followed by a partially proper morphism.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target. Partial properness and the canonical compactification Y′^{/Y} come from DiamondEtaleCohomology:C4. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/compactifiable-morphism is Huber's classical notion for adic spaces, not this one.

items.name: Proposition 22.3(i): compactifiable ⇔ separated with open canonical compactification
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y and Ỹ → Y be morphisms of v-stacks, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ. Then f is compactifiable if and only if it is separated and the natural map Y′ → Y′^{/Y} (the canonical compactification of Y′ over Y) is an open immersion.
items.note: S0: 'Prove ECD 22.3 using C4's canonical compactification: the equivalence with separatedness and the natural map being open, ...'. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.3(ii): compactifiability is stable under base change
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y and Ỹ → Y be morphisms of v-stacks, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ. If f is compactifiable, then f̃ is compactifiable.
items.note: S0 ('base change'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.3(iii): compactifiability is v-local on the target
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y and Ỹ → Y be morphisms of v-stacks, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ. If f̃ is compactifiable and Ỹ → Y is a surjective map of v-stacks, then f is compactifiable.
items.note: S0 ('v-locality on the target'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.3(iv): composites of compactifiable morphisms
items.statement: If Y₁ → Y₂ and Y₂ → Y₃ are compactifiable morphisms of v-stacks, then the composite Y₁ → Y₃ is compactifiable.
items.note: S0 ('composition'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.3(v): compactifiability is local on the source for open covers
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y and Ỹ → Y be morphisms of v-stacks, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ. If f is separated and representable in locally spatial diamonds and Y′ admits a cover by open subfunctors V ⊂ Y′ such that f|_V : V → Y is compactifiable, then f is compactifiable. Moreover, for any such open subfunctor V ⊂ Y′, the composite V → Y′ → Y′^{/Y} is an open immersion.
items.note: S0 ('open-locality on the source in the stated separated/representable scope'). Proof uses Proposition 10.5 over a strictly totally disconnected base. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.3(vi): separated étale maps are compactifiable
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y and Ỹ → Y be morphisms of v-stacks, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ. If f is separated and étale, then f is compactifiable.
items.note: S0 ('the separated étale case'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.3(vii): descent of compactifiability along locally split covers
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y and Ỹ → Y be morphisms of v-stacks, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ. If f is separated and representable in locally spatial diamonds and there is a separated surjective map g : Z → Y′ of v-stacks that after pullback to strictly totally disconnected spaces has local sections and such that f ∘ g is compactifiable, then f is compactifiable. (Hence, for separated maps representable in locally spatial diamonds, compactifiability is étale local on the source.)
items.note: S0 insists on storing the local-splitting hypothesis in every use; footnote 5 records that an earlier version without it was false (counterexamples), and whether universal openness of g suffices is open. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.3(viii): cancellation for compactifiable morphisms
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y and Ỹ → Y be morphisms of v-stacks, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ. If g : Y → Z is a separated map of v-stacks such that g ∘ f is compactifiable, then f is compactifiable.
items.note: S0 ('the cancellation statement'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Definition 22.4: Rf_! for compactifiable maps representable in spatial diamonds
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks which is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Write f as the composite of the open immersion j : Y′ ↪ Y′^{/Y} and the proper map f^{/Y} : Y′^{/Y} → Y (this factorisation exists for every quasicompact compactifiable map of small v-stacks). Then Rf_! := Rf^{/Y}_* ∘ j_! : D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ), where j_! is the extension by zero of Definition/Proposition 19.1.
items.locator: Definition 22.4, p. 129 (factorisation in the preceding paragraph), arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: S1: 'use the canonical factorization Y ↪ Ȳ → X and define Rf! = R f̄_* j!. The envelope Ȳ need not be spatial.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Theorem 22.5: cohomological dimension bound 3·dim.trg for the canonical compactification
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks which is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Write f = f^{/Y} ∘ j with j : Y′ ↪ Y′^{/Y} open and f^{/Y} : Y′^{/Y} → Y proper. Then Rf^{/Y}_* has bounded cohomological dimension: for all A ∈ D_ét(Y′^{/Y}, Λ) concentrated in degree 0, R^i f^{/Y}_* A = 0 for i > 3·dim.trg f. In particular, as j_* is exact (Remark 21.14), R^i f_* A = 0 for all A ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ) concentrated in degree 0 and i > 3·dim.trg f, so Rf_* has bounded cohomological dimension.
items.note: S1: 'Prove Theorem 22.5 in its actual strength ... R^i f̄_* = 0 for i > 3d ... Follow the reduction through its maximal Hausdorff quotient'. Proof inputs: Propositions 17.6, 19.2, 21.11, 21.16 (C8: nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C8/spatial-cohomological-bound, C8/point-cd-geometric-bound), 13.9/13.12/13.13 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/reduction-to-spatial-and-hausdorff-cohomology), 22.7 and [Sch92, Cor. 4.6] (C8/spectral-cohomological-bound). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Theorem 22.5, refinement: bound 2·dim.trg when the compactification is spatial
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 22.5, if f^{/Y} : Y′^{/Y} → Y is still representable in spatial diamonds, then R^i f^{/Y}_* A = 0 for i > 2·dim.trg f (A ∈ D_ét(Y′^{/Y}, Λ) in degree 0).
items.locator: Remark after Theorem 22.5, p. 130; first case of the proof, p. 130, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: S1: 'The improved 2d bound has the additional spatiality hypothesis on the canonical compactification.' The proof reduces to Y = Spa(C,C⁺), uses Theorem 19.2 to kill j_!j^*A and Propositions 21.11, 21.16. The paper notes it does not know whether the canonical compactification of a spatial map is spatial (C4 forbids asserting it). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.6: proper diamonds of dim.trg 0 over strictly totally disconnected bases
items.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space. Then the category of proper diamonds f : Y → X with dim.trg f = 0 is equivalent to the category of compact Hausdorff spaces over π₀X, via sending a compact Hausdorff space T → π₀X to X ×_{π₀X} T. In particular, if X = Spa(C, C⁺), the category of proper diamonds f : Y → X with dim.trg f = 0 is equivalent to the category of compact Hausdorff spaces.
items.note: S1: 'prove Propositions 22.6–22.7 on proper dim.trg = 0 diamonds over strictly totally disconnected spaces'. Proof uses Example 11.12 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.7: D⁺_ét of a proper dim.trg-0 diamond is D⁺ of its topological space
items.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space and f : Y → X a proper map of diamonds of dim.trg f = 0, so that Y = X ×_{π₀X} T for some compact Hausdorff space T → π₀X (Proposition 22.6). Then pullback under Y → |Y| defines an equivalence D⁺(|Y|, Λ) ≃ D⁺_ét(Y, Λ), where D⁺(|Y|, Λ) is the derived category of sheaves of Λ-modules on the topological space |Y|.
items.note: S1 ('Include ... the comparison of ordinary topological sheaves used in this reduction'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Claim in the proof of Proposition 22.7: continuity of cohomology along cofiltered limits of qcqs diamonds
items.statement: For any small v-sheaf Y and C ∈ D⁺_ét(Y, Λ), and any cofiltered inverse system of qcqs diamonds Z_i → Y with inverse limit Z, one has RΓ(Z, C) = colim_i RΓ(Z_i, C).
items.note: Planned only as part of the proof of 22.7 (S1). Proved from Proposition 14.9 (spatial case; DiamondEtaleCohomology:C0 'continuity of étale cohomology') plus Lemma 11.22 and Proposition 12.3 descent. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.8: base change for Rf_! (spatial, finite dim.trg)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks which is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let g : Ỹ → Y be any map of small v-stacks, with base change f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ and g′ : Ỹ′ → Y′. There is a natural base change equivalence g^* Rf_! ≃ Rf̃_! g′^* of functors D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Ỹ, Λ).
items.note: S1: 'Prove 22.8–22.12: base change, composition, agreement with the étale left adjoint, projection formula, and preservation of coproducts.' Proof: Theorem 22.5 + Proposition 17.6 + Proposition 19.1. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.9: composition of Rf_! (spatial, finite dim.trg)
items.statement: Let g : Y″ → Y′ and f : Y′ → Y be compactifiable maps of small v-stacks which are representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f, dim.trg g < ∞, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Then there is a natural equivalence Rf_! ∘ Rg_! ≃ R(f ∘ g)_! of functors D_ét(Y″, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ).
items.note: S1 (22.8–22.12). Proof via Theorem 19.2 and Theorem 22.5. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.10: agreement with the étale left adjoint (quasicompact case)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a quasicompact separated étale map of small v-stacks, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Then Rf_! as defined in Definition 19.1 (the left adjoint of f^*) agrees with Rf_! as defined in Definition 22.4.
items.note: S1 ('agreement with the étale left adjoint'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.11: projection formula (spatial, finite dim.trg)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-sheaves which is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞, and let Λ be a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Then there is a functorial isomorphism Rf_! B ⊗^L_Λ A ≃ Rf_!(B ⊗^L_Λ f^* A) in B ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ) and A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ).
items.note: S1 ('For the projection formula, use A on the base and B on the source'). Proof uses Theorem 19.2 and Proposition 22.12. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.12: Rf_! commutes with direct sums (spatial, finite dim.trg)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-sheaves which is representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞, and let Λ be a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Then for any collection of objects A_i ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ), i ∈ I (I a set), the natural map ⊕_i Rf_! A_i → Rf_!(⊕_i A_i) is an isomorphism in D_ét(Y, Λ).
items.note: S1 ('preservation of coproducts'). Proof uses Proposition 22.8, the 3·dim.trg bound and [SGA 4 VI, Cor. 5.2] (cohomology on the coherent v-topos of a qcqs v-sheaf commutes with filtered colimits). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Definition 22.13(a): sheaves with proper support over Y, D_{ét,prop/Y}(Y′, Λ)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of quasiseparated locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let j : Y′ ↪ Y′^{/Y} and f^{/Y} : Y′^{/Y} → Y (partially proper) be the usual maps. D_{ét,prop/Y}(Y′, Λ) ⊂ D_ét(Y′, Λ) is the full ∞-subcategory of those A with A ≃ j_{V!} j_V^* A for some open subspace j_V : V ↪ Y′ that is quasicompact over Y.
items.note: S2: 'Define the full enhanced subcategory of objects of the form j_V! j_V* A with V an open subspace quasicompact over the target.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Definition 22.13(b): Rf_! for quasiseparated locally spatial diamonds by left Kan extension
items.statement: In the situation of Definition 22.13(a), Rf_! : D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ) is the left Kan extension of Rf^{/Y}_* j_! : D_{ét,prop/Y}(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ) along the full inclusion D_{ét,prop/Y}(Y′, Λ) ⊂ D_ét(Y′, Λ). Writing A as the filtered colimit of A_V = j_{V!} j_V^* A over opens V quasicompact over Y, Rf_! A = colim_V Rf_! A_V, and Rf_! A_V = R(f|_V)_!(j_V^* A) (Definition 22.4).
items.locator: Definition 22.13 and following paragraph, p. 135, arXiv:1709.07343v4
items.note: S2: 'Define Rf! by left Kan extension from this subcategory (22.13) ... Do not replace the Kan extension by an ordinary unstructured choice of representatives'. Kan extension theory: EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/left-kan-extension-along-a-full-inclusion. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.14: Rf_! commutes with colimits (quasiseparated locally spatial case)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of quasiseparated locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. The functor Rf_! : D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ) commutes with all direct sums; equivalently ([Lur16, Prop. 1.4.4.1(2)]), with all colimits.
items.note: S2 ('its filtered-support formula, colimit preservation and base change (22.14–22.15)'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.15: base change for Rf_! (quasiseparated locally spatial case)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of quasiseparated locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let g : Ỹ → Y be any map of locally spatial diamonds, with base change f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ and g′ : Ỹ′ → Y′. There is a natural base change equivalence g^* Rf_! ≃ Rf̃_! g′^* of functors D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Ỹ, Λ).
items.note: S2 (22.14–22.15). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Construction of Rf^0_{•!} over a simplicial v-hypercover (before Lemma 22.16)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, nΛ = 0 (n prime to p). Choose a simplicial v-hypercover Y_• → Y with all Y_i quasiseparated locally spatial diamonds and put Y′_• = Y′ ×_Y Y_•. The assignment i ↦ D_ét(Y′_i, Λ) (pullback functors; [LZ14, §2]) is encoded by a coCartesian fibration D_ét(Y′_•, Λ)^0 → Δ whose ∞-category of sections is D_ét(Y′_•, Λ); the full subcategory D_{ét,prop/Y_•}(Y′_•, Λ)^0 with fibres D_{ét,prop/Y_i}(Y′_i, Λ) is again coCartesian; j_•^* : D_ét(Y′_•^{/Y_•}, Λ)^0 → D_ét(Y′_•, Λ)^0 has a fully faithful left adjoint j_{•!} (fibrewise j_{i!}); Rf^{/Y_•}_{•*} is right adjoint to f^{/Y_•,*}_• (fibrewise Rf^{/Y_i}_{i*}). Rf^0_{•!} : D_ét(Y′_•, Λ)^0 → D_ét(Y_•, Λ)^0 is the left Kan extension of Rf^{/Y_•}_{•*} j_{•!} : D_{ét,prop/Y_•}(Y′_•, Λ)^0 → D_ét(Y_•, Λ)^0, which exists by [Lur09, Cor. 4.3.2.14].
items.note: S2: 'choose a simplicial v-hypercover ... Construct the coherent diagram of coefficient categories and support subcategories. Apply E3's fibrewise left Kan extension theorem'. Inputs: EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0/cocartesian-fibrations-and-restricted-straightening, E3/coherent-diagrams-of-ringed-topoi, E3/left-kan-extension-along-a-full-inclusion. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Lemma 22.16: fibres of Rf^0_{•!}
items.statement: The functor Rf^0_{•!} is given by Rf_{i!} : D_ét(Y′_i, Λ) → D_ét(Y_i, Λ) (Definition 22.13) in the fibre over i ∈ Δ.
items.note: S2 ('prove 22.16'); cofinality input [Lur09, Prop. 4.3.1.7] (E3). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Lemma 22.17: Rf^0_{•!} preserves coCartesian edges
items.statement: The functor Rf^0_{•!} : D_ét(Y′_•, Λ)^0 → D_ét(Y_•, Λ)^0 sends coCartesian edges to coCartesian edges.
items.note: S2 ('then prove preservation of coCartesian edges (22.17)'); proof from Lemma 22.16 and Proposition 22.15. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Definition 22.18: Rf_! for compactifiable maps of small v-stacks
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. The functor Rf_! : D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ) is obtained by passing to coCartesian sections, D_ét(Y′, Λ) ≃ D_{ét,cart}(Y′_•, Λ) → D_{ét,cart}(Y_•, Λ) ≃ D_ét(Y, Λ) via Rf^0_{•!}, and then to homotopy categories. It is independent of the choice of the simplicial v-hypercover (by passing to common refinements).
items.note: S2: 'Descend along the hypercover to construct 22.18. Prove independence of the cover through common refinements and compatible equivalences.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.19: base change for Rf_! (general)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks which is representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Let g : Ỹ → Y be any map of small v-stacks, with base change f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ and g′ : Ỹ′ → Y′. There is a natural base change equivalence g^* Rf_! ≃ Rf̃_! g′^* of functors D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Ỹ, Λ).
items.note: S2 ('Prove base change 22.19 ... at the enhanced level'); this is Theorem 1.9(ii) of the introduction. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.20: Rf_! commutes with all colimits (general)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. The functor Rf_! : D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ) commutes with all direct sums; equivalently ([Lur16, Prop. 1.4.4.1(2)]), with all colimits.
items.note: S2 ('colimit preservation 22.20'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.21: composition of Rf_! (general)
items.statement: Let g : Y″ → Y′ and f : Y′ → Y be compactifiable maps of small v-stacks which are representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f, dim.trg g < ∞, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Then there is a natural equivalence Rf_! ∘ Rg_! ≃ R(f ∘ g)_! of functors D_ét(Y″, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ).
items.note: S2 ('composition 22.21'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.22: agreement with the étale left adjoint (general)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated étale map of small v-stacks, and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Then Rf_! as defined in Definition 19.1 agrees with Rf_! as defined in Definition 22.18.
items.note: S2 ('étale agreement 22.22'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 22.23: projection formula (general)
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-sheaves which is representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, and let Λ be a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Then there is a functorial isomorphism Rf_! B ⊗^L_Λ A ≃ Rf_!(B ⊗^L_Λ f^* A) in B ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ) and A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ).
items.note: S2 ('projection formula 22.23 ... In results printed first for v-sheaves, include the explicit hyperdescent passage needed for the small-v-stack formulation advertised in the introduction' — Theorem 1.8(iii) cites 22.23 for small v-stacks). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Theorem 23.1: existence of the right adjoint Rf^!
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks which is representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, and let Λ be a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Then Rf_! : D_ét(Y′, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ) admits a right adjoint Rf^! : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ).
items.note: S3: 'Use presentability and colimit preservation to construct the enhanced right adjoint Rf^! to Rf! (23.1).' Proof: [Lur09, Cor. 5.5.2.9] (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/adjoint-functor-theorem-and-localisations) + Proposition 22.20. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Remark 23.2: Rf^! commutes with restriction of scalars
items.statement: Let f be as in Theorem 23.1 and g : Λ′ → Λ a map of such coefficient rings, inducing restriction of scalars D_ét(−, Λ) → D_ét(−, Λ′). Then restriction of scalars intertwines Rf^! for Λ and Rf^! for Λ′ (the square with Rf^! : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ) on top and Rf^! : D_ét(Y, Λ′) → D_ét(Y′, Λ′) on the bottom commutes); it is the right adjoint of the identity Rf_!(− ⊗_{Λ′} Λ) = Rf_!(−) ⊗_{Λ′} Λ, a consequence of the projection formula 22.23.
items.note: S3: 'Prove coefficient restriction compatibility (23.2)'. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.3(i): Verdier duality for Rf_!
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, and let Λ be a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For all A ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ), B ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ): RHom_Λ(Rf_! A, B) ≅ Rf_* RHom_Λ(A, Rf^! B).
items.note: S3: 'the two internal-Hom adjunction identities (23.3)'; = Theorem 1.8(iv). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.3(ii): Rf^! of internal Hom
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, and let Λ be a ring with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. For all A, B ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ): Rf^! RHom_Λ(A, B) ≅ RHom_Λ(f^* A, Rf^! B).
items.note: S3 (23.3); = Theorem 1.8(v). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.4: criteria for Rf^! to be a twisted pullback over a strictly totally disconnected base
items.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space, let f : Y → X be a compactifiable map from a locally spatial diamond Y of locally dim.trg f < ∞, and fix a prime ℓ ≠ p. The following are equivalent. (i) The natural transformation Rf^!F_ℓ ⊗_{F_ℓ} f^* → Rf^! : D_ét(X, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y, F_ℓ), adjoint to Rf_!(Rf^!F_ℓ ⊗_{F_ℓ} f^*−) = Rf_!Rf^!F_ℓ ⊗_{F_ℓ} id → id (projection formula 22.23), is an equivalence. (ii) Rf^! : D_ét(X, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y, F_ℓ) is equivalent to a functor A ⊗_{F_ℓ} f^* for some A ∈ D_ét(Y, F_ℓ). (iii) Rf^! commutes with arbitrary direct sums, and for all connected components X₀ = Spa(C, C⁺) ⊂ X with an open subset j : U ⊂ X₀ and pullbacks f_U : V → U, f₀ : Y₀ → X₀, j′ : V → Y₀, the map j′_! Rf_U^! F_ℓ → Rf₀^! j_! F_ℓ adjoint to Rf₀_! j′_! Rf_U^! F_ℓ = j_! Rf_{U!} Rf_U^! F_ℓ → j_! F_ℓ is an equivalence. (iv) For all affinoid pro-étale maps g : X′ → X with pullback f′ : Y′ → X′, h : Y′ → Y, the natural transformation h^* Rf^! → Rf′^! g^* : D_ét(X, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y′, F_ℓ) adjoint to Rf′_! h^* Rf^! = g^* Rf_! Rf^! → g^* is an equivalence, and for all X₀, U, j as in (iii) the natural transformation j′_! Rf_U^! → Rf₀^! j_! : D_ét(U, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y₀, F_ℓ) adjoint to Rf₀_! j′_! Rf_U^! = j_! Rf_{U!} Rf_U^! → j_! is an equivalence.
items.note: S4: 'Prove 23.4–23.7, including the equivalences of criteria over strictly totally disconnected bases'. The printed proof uses 23.16(i) (planned in S3 precisely for this reason) and Lemma 23.6. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.4, final assertion: ℓ-power-torsion coefficients
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 23.4, under the equivalent conditions (i)–(iv), for any ℓ-power-torsion ring Λ the natural transformation Rf^!Λ ⊗_Λ f^* → Rf^! : D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ) is an equivalence.
items.note: S4 (23.4). Proof reduces to Λ = Z/ℓ^m Z via Remark 23.2 and uses self-injectivity of Z/ℓ^m Z. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Lemma 23.6: pushforward along a profinite projection
items.statement: Let S be a profinite set, let Y be a small v-sheaf, and consider h : Y × S → Y. Then for any ring Λ and any C ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ), one has a natural isomorphism Rh_* h^* C ≃ C⁰(S, Λ) ⊗_Λ C, where C⁰(S, Λ) is the Λ-module of continuous maps S → Λ.
items.note: S4: 'the profinite-projection calculation'. The printed proof uses Definition 22.4 and the projection formula 22.11, valid only for nΛ = 0 with n prime to p (see sourceIssues). C⁰(S, Λ) corresponds to Mathlib's LocallyConstant S Λ, but the lemma itself is not in any library. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.7: Rf^! preserves direct sums iff Rf_! preserves constructibility
items.statement: Let X be a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space, f : Y → X a compactifiable map from a spatial diamond Y with dim.trg f < ∞, and fix a prime ℓ ≠ p. The functor Rf^! : D_ét(X, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y, F_ℓ) commutes with arbitrary direct sums if and only if for all constructible sheaves F of F_ℓ-vector spaces on Y_ét and all i ≥ 0, the !-pushforward R^i f_! F is constructible on X_ét.
items.note: S4 ('the compactness/direct-sum criterion'). Inputs: Theorem 22.5, Proposition 20.10 (C9 nodes DiamondEtaleCohomology:C9/compact-generators, C9/finite-field-compact-objects) and Neeman's observation [Nee96] (missing, see separate item). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Definition 23.8 (second paragraph): invertible objects of D_ét(Y, F_ℓ)
items.statement: For a locally spatial diamond Y, an object D ∈ D_ét(Y, F_ℓ) is invertible if it is locally (equivalently, in the v-, quasi-pro-étale, or étale topology of Y) isomorphic to F_ℓ[n] for some integer n ∈ Z.
items.note: S4 ('tensor with an invertible object followed by pullback'). Tau Ceti has invertible sheaves of modules (TauCeti/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Sheaf/Invertible) but not this derived étale notion. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Definition 23.8: ℓ-cohomologically smooth morphism
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds, and let ℓ ≠ p be a prime. Then f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth if f is compactifiable, locally dim.trg f < ∞, and for any strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space X with a map X → Y and pullback f_X : Y′ ×_Y X → X, the functor Rf_X^! : D_ét(X, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Y′ ×_Y X, F_ℓ) is equivalent to a functor of the form D_{f_X} ⊗_{F_ℓ} f_X^* for some invertible object D_{f_X} ∈ D_ét(Y′ ×_Y X, F_ℓ). (It is not required a priori that the equivalence be natural or that D_{f_X} commute with base change; these follow from Proposition 23.12.)
items.note: S4: 'Define ℓ-cohomological smoothness exactly as in 23.8'. Printed with f^* for f_X^* (see sourceIssues). Consumers: VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS0/shriek-pullback-for-smooth-stacky-maps extends it to stacky maps (FS IV.1). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.10: practical criterion for ℓ-cohomological smoothness
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a compactifiable map of small v-stacks which is representable in spatial diamonds, and let ℓ ≠ p be a prime. Then f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth if and only if: (i) dim.trg f < ∞; (ii) for any strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space X with a map g : X → Y and pullback f_X : Y′ ×_Y X → X, and any constructible étale sheaf F of F_ℓ-vector spaces on the spatial diamond Y′ ×_Y X, R^i f_{X!} F is constructible on X for all i ≥ 0; (iii) for any X = Spa(C, C⁺) (C algebraically closed, C⁺ ⊂ C open and bounded valuation subring) with a map to Y and a quasicompact open subset j : U → X, with pullbacks f_U : Y′ ×_Y U → U, f_X, j′ : Y′ ×_Y U → Y′ ×_Y X, the natural map j′_! Rf_U^! F_ℓ → Rf_X^! j_! F_ℓ adjoint to Rf_{X!} j′_! Rf_U^! F_ℓ = j_! Rf_{U!} Rf_U^! F_ℓ → j_! F_ℓ is an equivalence; (iv) for any strictly totally disconnected perfectoid X with a map g : X → Y and pullback f_X, the !-pullback Rf_X^! F_ℓ ∈ D_ét(Y′ ×_Y X, F_ℓ) is invertible.
items.note: S4 ('(23.10–23.12)'). Proof from 23.4 ((ii)⇔(iii)) and 23.7. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.11: ℓ-cohomologically smooth maps are universally open
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth for some ℓ ≠ p. Then f is universally open, i.e. for all X → Y the map |Y′ ×_Y X| → |X| is open.
items.note: S4 ('Prove universal openness'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.12(i): Rf^! is a twist of pullback; the dualizing complex is invertible
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds such that f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and let Λ be an ℓ-power-torsion ring. The natural transformation Rf^!Λ ⊗_Λ f^* → Rf^! : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ) is an equivalence, and the dualizing complex D_f := Rf^!Λ ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ) is invertible, in fact étale locally isomorphic to Λ[n] for some integer n ∈ Z.
items.note: S4: 'Prove that the a priori unspecified equivalence becomes the canonical tensor transformation and that the dualizing object is Rf^!Λ'. Proved jointly with (iii). = Theorem 1.10(i). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.12(ii): quasicompact smooth Rf_! preserves perfect-constructible complexes
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds such that f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and let Λ be an ℓ-power-torsion ring. If f is quasicompact, then for any perfect-constructible A ∈ D_ét(Y′, Λ), the proper pushforward Rf_! A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ) is perfect-constructible.
items.note: S4: 'preservation of perfect-constructible complexes under quasicompact cohomologically smooth Rf!'. Uses Proposition 20.17 (C9/compact-iff-perfect-constructible). = Theorem 1.11 for Λ = F_ℓ. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.12(iii): Rf^! commutes with arbitrary base change for smooth f
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds such that f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and let Λ be an ℓ-power-torsion ring. If g : Ỹ → Y is a map of small v-sheaves with base change f̃ : Ỹ′ → Ỹ and g′ : Ỹ′ → Y′, then the natural transformation g′^* Rf^! → Rf̃^! g^* : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Ỹ′, Λ), adjoint to Rf̃_! g′^* Rf^! = g^* Rf_! Rf^! → g^*, is an equivalence. In particular the dualizing complex commutes with base change: g′^* D_f = D_f̃.
items.note: S4 ('base change of the dualizing object'). Proof via a v-hypercover and Proposition 17.3. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.13 (first part): composites of ℓ-cohomologically smooth maps
items.statement: Let g : Y″ → Y′ and f : Y′ → Y be separated morphisms of small v-stacks and ℓ ≠ p a prime. If f and g are representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth, then f ∘ g is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth.
items.note: S4 ('Prove composition'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.13 (second part): smoothness descends along smooth surjections
items.statement: Let g : Y″ → Y′ and f : Y′ → Y be separated morphisms of small v-stacks and ℓ ≠ p a prime. If g and f ∘ g are representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth, g is surjective, and f is representable in diamonds and compactifiable, then f is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth.
items.note: S4: 'the precise reverse implication of 23.13 ... keep the assumptions that the intermediate map is representable in diamonds and compactifiable, as well as surjectivity'. The paper (p. 150) notes compactifiability of f can be dropped when g has local sections after pullback to strictly totally disconnected spaces (22.3(vii)), e.g. when g is formally smooth ([FS26, Def. IV.3.1, Prop. IV.3.5]). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Remark 23.14: representability in locally spatial diamonds descends along universally open covers
items.statement: If f : Y′ → Y is a separated 0-truncated map of small v-stacks that is representable in diamonds, and g : Y″ → Y′ is a universally open (e.g. ℓ-cohomologically smooth), separated and surjective map of small v-stacks such that f ∘ g is representable in locally spatial diamonds, then f is representable in locally spatial diamonds.
items.note: Nearest layer: DiamondSixOperations:S4 plans 23.13, whose proof contains the smooth case of this argument (via 23.11, Proposition 13.4 and Lemma 2.10); no stage or node states the universally-open generalisation. DiamondsAndVStacks:D5 owns relative representability but does not state it.

items.name: Proposition 23.15 (first part): ℓ-cohomological smoothness is stable under base change
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds, and ℓ ≠ p a prime. Let g : Ỹ → Y be a map of small v-stacks with pullback f̃ : Ỹ′ = Y′ ×_Y Ỹ → Ỹ. If f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, then f̃ is ℓ-cohomologically smooth.
items.note: S4. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.15 (converse): ℓ-cohomological smoothness is v-local on the target
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 23.15, if f̃ is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, g is a surjective map of v-stacks, and locally dim.trg f < ∞, then f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth.
items.note: S4: 'Prove target v-descent as in 23.15, retaining local finiteness of dim.trg f as an assumption on f itself' (the paper says it is unclear whether that condition is v-local). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.16(i): Rg^! commutes with pushforward
items.statement: Let Y′ →(g̃) Y, f′ : Y′ → X′, f : Y → X, g : X′ → X be a cartesian diagram of small v-stacks (Y′ = X′ ×_X Y), and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Assume that g is compactifiable and representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg g < ∞, and A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ). Then Rg^! Rf_* A ≅ Rf′_* Rg̃^! A.
items.note: S3: 'prove the formal exceptional base-change identity 23.16(i) by taking right adjoints of 22.19 ... used earlier in the printed proof of 23.4'. = Theorem 1.9(iii). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.16(ii): smooth base change
items.statement: Let Y′ →(g̃) Y, f′ : Y′ → X′, f : Y → X, g : X′ → X be a cartesian diagram of small v-stacks (Y′ = X′ ×_X Y), and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Assume that g is separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and Λ is ℓ-power torsion. Then for all A ∈ D_ét(Y, Λ), the base change morphism g^* Rf_* A → Rf′_* g̃^* A is an isomorphism.
items.note: S4 ('Prove smooth base change and the remaining identities of 23.16–23.17'). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.16(iii): Rf^! commutes with smooth base change
items.statement: Let Y′ →(g̃) Y, f′ : Y′ → X′, f : Y → X, g : X′ → X be a cartesian diagram of small v-stacks (Y′ = X′ ×_X Y), and assume nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p. Assume that g is separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and Λ is ℓ-power torsion [and, implicitly, that f is compactifiable and representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally dim.trg f < ∞, so that Rf^! and Rf′^! are defined]. Then for all A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ), the map g̃^* Rf^! A → Rf′^! g^* A adjoint to Rf^! A → Rf^! Rg_* g^* A = Rg̃_* Rf′^! g^* A is an equivalence.
items.note: S4: 'when applying 23.16(iii), provide the hypotheses making the vertical map's exceptional inverse image available, rather than relying on an ill-typed standalone formula' (hypothesis omitted in print; see sourceIssues). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 23.17: smooth pullback commutes with internal Hom
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth [and Λ ℓ-power torsion, as in Theorem 1.10(ii); omitted in print]. There is a functorial isomorphism f^* RHom(A, B) ≅ RHom(f^* A, f^* B) in A, B ∈ D_ét(X, Λ).
items.note: S4 ('the remaining identities of 23.16–23.17'). Proof: 23.3(ii) and 23.12(i). No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: The ball B (Theorem 24.1)
items.statement: B is the v-sheaf on Perf with B(R, R⁺) = R⁺ (the absolute perfectoid closed unit ball), and f : B → * the projection to the point.
items.note: S5: 'Prove Theorem 24.1 for the absolute perfectoid-ball functor B(R,R⁺) = R⁺. After perfectoid base change this is the perfected ball.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Theorem 24.1: the ball is ℓ-cohomologically smooth with dualizing complex Λ(1)[2]
items.statement: Let f : B → * be the projection from the ball to the point, where B(R, R⁺) = R⁺. Then f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth for any prime ℓ ≠ p, and for any ring Λ with nΛ = 0 for some n prime to p, one has a canonical isomorphism D_f = Rf^!Λ ≅ Λ(1)[2].
items.note: S5: 'Use H3's curve trace/duality and H4's relative constructibility input to obtain the canonical normalization Rf^!Λ ≃ Λ(1)[2]'. Classical inputs: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/relative-ball-compact-support, H3/curve-trace, H3/curve-poincare-duality, H3/duality-open-extension-compatibility, H3/lower-shriek-cohomological-dimension; H4 (Hub96 6.2.2, stage only). The printed proof treats Λ = F_ℓ; the passage to general Λ with nΛ = 0 is not written out. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 24.2: quotients by free profinite actions of pro-order prime to ℓ
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth for some prime ℓ ≠ p. Assume that there is a profinite group K of pro-order prime to ℓ with a free action K × Y′ → Y′ over Y, i.e. such that K × Y′ → Y′ ×_Y Y′ is an injection. Then the quotient map f/K : Y′/K → Y is separated, representable in locally spatial diamonds, and ℓ-cohomologically smooth. Moreover, fixing the Λ-valued Haar measure on K with total volume 1 [Λ implicitly ℓ-power torsion, so that the indices [K : H] are invertible], there is a natural equivalence of functors Rf^! = q^* R(f/K)^! : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ), where q : Y′ → Y′/K is the quotient map.
items.note: S5: 'Prove 24.2 for free actions of a profinite group of pro-order prime to ℓ, including the normalized Λ-valued Haar measure and compatibility of finite-level traces.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Remark after Proposition 24.2: Rq^! is not q^*
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 24.2 one also has Rf^! = Rq^! R(f/K)^!, but Rq^! ≠ q^* in general: after a base change q becomes S × Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C, O_C) for a profinite set S and an algebraically closed perfectoid field C, and then Rq^!Λ is the sheaf sending an open and closed T ⊂ S to the distributions Hom(C⁰(T, Λ), Λ). A choice of Haar measure gives a natural map q^* → Rq^!.
items.note: Nearest layer: DiamondSixOperations:S5 mentions this only as a caution ('do not assert Rq^! = q^*: the source explicitly describes a distribution-valued counterexample'); computing Rq^!Λ as distributions is not a stated target. The Haar-measure map q^* → Rq^! is part of the planned proof of 24.2.

items.name: Proposition 24.3: quotients by non-free profinite actions with smooth geometric fibres
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated map of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds and ℓ-cohomologically smooth for some prime ℓ ≠ p. Assume that there is a profinite group K of pro-order prime to ℓ with an action K × Y′ → Y′ over Y for which the map K × Y′ → Y′ ×_Y Y′ is 0-truncated and qcqs. Let Y′/K be the quotient of Y′ by the equivalence relation given as the image of K × Y′ → Y′ ×_Y Y′. Then f/K : Y′/K → Y is separated and representable in locally spatial diamonds. Moreover, if for all complete algebraically closed fields C with an open and bounded valuation subring C⁺ ⊂ C and all maps Spa(C, C⁺) → Y the pullback Y′/K ×_Y Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, then f/K is ℓ-cohomologically smooth, and, fixing the Λ-valued Haar measure on K with total volume 1, there is a natural equivalence Rf^! = q^* R(f/K)^! : D_ét(Y, Λ) → D_ét(Y′, Λ), where q : Y′ → Y′/K is the quotient map.
items.note: S5: 'Prove 24.3 in the nonfree case with its 0-truncated qcqs image-relation and fibrewise smoothness hypotheses. It is needed in the mixed-characteristic argument'. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Smooth morphism of analytic adic spaces and relative ball B^n_Y (Proposition 24.4)
items.statement: A separated morphism f : Y′ → Y of analytic adic spaces over Spa Z_p is smooth if it is locally on Y′ the composition of an étale map Y′ → B^n_Y and the projection B^n_Y → Y (cf. [Hub96, Cor. 1.6.10]); for Y = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid, B^n_Y = Spa(A⟨T₁, …, T_n⟩, A⁺⟨T₁, …, T_n⟩).
items.note: Node AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/smooth-morphism-ball-charts: 'This is the notion smooth of ECD Proposition 24.4 for analytic adic spaces over Spa ℤ_p'; comparison with Huber's smoothness: A2/smooth-local-ball-charts.

items.name: Proposition 24.4: smooth morphisms of analytic adic spaces are ℓ-cohomologically smooth
items.statement: Let f : Y′ → Y be a separated smooth morphism of analytic adic spaces over Spa Z_p, i.e. f is locally on Y′ the composition of an étale map Y′ → B^n_Y and the projection B^n_Y → Y. Then f^♢ : (Y′)^♢ → Y^♢ is ℓ-cohomologically smooth (for every prime ℓ ≠ p).
items.note: S5: 'Deduce 24.4 for separated smooth analytic adic morphisms over ℤ_p by local ball/torus presentations, characteristic-p comparison and the compatible-root ℤ_p-quotient argument.' Uses Lemma 15.6 (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/diamond-of-analytic-adic-space-and-etale-site-15-6), 22.3, 23.13, 24.1–24.3. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 24.5: (Spa Q_p)^♢ → * is ℓ-cohomologically smooth
items.statement: The map (Spa Q_p)^♢ → * is ℓ-cohomologically smooth (ℓ ≠ p).
items.note: S5: 'Deduce 24.5 for Spd ℚ_p → * using the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension and the punctured perfectoid disc.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 24.6: smoothness criterion over a general perfectoid base
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid space, let Y be a locally spatial diamond, and let f : Y → X be compactifiable with locally dim.trg f < ∞. Then f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth if and only if (i) the sheaf Rf^!F_ℓ ∈ D_ét(Y, F_ℓ) is invertible, i.e. étale locally isomorphic to F_ℓ[d] for some d ∈ Z; and (ii) for any X̃ → X that is an open subset of a finite-dimensional ball B^n_X over X, with pullback f̃ : Ỹ = Y ×_X X̃ → X̃, the natural transformation Rf̃^!F_ℓ ⊗^L_{F_ℓ} f̃^* → Rf̃^! of functors D_ét(X̃, F_ℓ) → D_ét(Ỹ, F_ℓ) is an equivalence.
items.note: S5: 'Prove the alternate geometric-base criterion 24.6.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Theorem 25.1: biduality over Spa(C, O_C)
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of characteristic p with ring of integers O_C, and let X be a locally spatial diamond that is separated and ℓ-cohomologically smooth over Spa(C, O_C) (structure map f) for some ℓ ≠ p. Let A ∈ D_ét(X, F_ℓ) be a bounded complex with constructible cohomology. Then the double (naive) duality map A → RHom_{F_ℓ}(RHom_{F_ℓ}(A, F_ℓ), F_ℓ) is an equivalence; equivalently, as Rf^!F_ℓ is invertible, the double Verdier duality map A → RHom_{F_ℓ}(RHom_{F_ℓ}(A, Rf^!F_ℓ), Rf^!F_ℓ) is an equivalence.
items.note: S6: 'Prove Theorem 25.1 ... Follow the reduction to j!𝔽_ℓ, strict-localization/approximation, the ball, and H5's smooth-curve compactification, keeping the actual biduality map throughout.' Inputs: Propositions 20.7, 20.8, 20.10, 23.17, Theorem 24.1, [Lüt95, Thm 5.3] (H5), Poincaré duality for curves (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/curve-poincare-duality). = Theorem 1.12. Nearest scheme analogue: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.1:biduality. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Theorem 25.1 (final assertion): finiteness of cohomology
items.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of characteristic p with ring of integers O_C, and let X be a locally spatial diamond that is separated and ℓ-cohomologically smooth over Spa(C, O_C) (structure map f) for some ℓ ≠ p. Let A ∈ D_ét(X, F_ℓ) be a bounded complex with constructible cohomology. If moreover X is quasicompact, then H^i(X, A) is finite for all i ∈ Z.
items.note: S6: 'Prove biduality and the finiteness of cohomology when X is quasicompact.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Remark 25.2: biduality fails over Spa(C, C⁺) with C⁺ ≠ O_C
items.statement: Theorem 25.1 does not hold with Spa(C, O_C) replaced by Spa(C, C⁺), C⁺ ≠ O_C, even for X = Spa(C, C⁺): if j : U = Spa(C, O_C) ↪ X denotes the open immersion, then A = j_!F_ℓ has dual RHom_{F_ℓ}(j_!F_ℓ, F_ℓ) = Rj_*F_ℓ = j_*F_ℓ = F_ℓ, so the double dual is F_ℓ, which is different from A = j_!F_ℓ.
items.note: S6: 'Implement the counterexample of Remark 25.2 over Spa(C,C⁺) with C⁺ ≠ 𝒪_C'. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Remark 25.3: biduality and perfectness for ℓ-power-torsion coefficients
items.statement: Let C, X be as in Theorem 25.1 and Λ an ℓ-power-torsion ring. The biduality theorem also holds for perfect-constructible A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ), and in that case RΓ(X, A) is a perfect complex of Λ-modules if X is quasicompact.
items.note: S6: 'Prove the perfect-constructible extension to general ℓ-power-torsion commutative coefficients in Remark 25.3 ... The resulting perfect global-sections complex is a complex of coefficient-ring modules' (the print says 'A-modules'; see sourceIssues). Uses Proposition 20.17. No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Proposition 25.4: conservativity of Verdier duality over Spa(C, O_C)
items.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of characteristic p with ring of integers O_C, and let X be a locally spatial diamond with f : X → Spa(C, O_C) compactifiable with locally dim.trg f < ∞. If A ∈ D_ét(X, F_ℓ) satisfies RHom_{F_ℓ}(A, Rf^!F_ℓ) = 0, then A = 0.
items.note: S6: 'Prove the Verdier dual conservativity assertion 25.4 in its stated compactifiable finite-dimensional setting.' No DiamondSixOperations packet or reviewed decomposition exists, so there are no nodes; the stage description states this target.

items.name: Remark 25.5: conservativity fails over Spa(C, C⁺) with C⁺ ≠ O_C
items.statement: For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C⁺ ≠ O_C and i : {s} → X the inclusion of the closed point, RHom_Λ(i_*Λ, Λ) = 0 although i_*Λ ≠ 0.
items.note: Nearest layer: DiamondSixOperations:S6 implements the analogous biduality counterexample (Remark 25.2) but does not name this one.

items.name: Remark 25.6: conservativity for general coefficient rings (conditional)
items.statement: A result similar to Proposition 25.4 holds with coefficients in a ring Λ killed by n prime to p as soon as every M ∈ D(Λ) with RHom_Λ(M, Λ) = 0 is zero. This fails in some cases, e.g. for Λ = O_K with K spherically complete and M = k the residue field.
items.note: Nearest layer: DiamondSixOperations:S6 only records that 'the general-ring conservativity discussion in Remark 25.6 is conditional, not an unconditional extension'; neither the conditional statement nor the counterexample is a stated target.

items.name: Adic coefficient rings (§26 setup)
items.statement: Λ is a ring complete for, and equipped with, the I-adic topology for a finitely generated ideal I ⊂ Λ; for simplicity I is assumed to be generated by a regular sequence and to contain an integer prime to p.
